1	# Morsel — Design & Architecture Specification
2	
3	> **Version:** 0.39 · **Status:** Draft · **Date:** May 2026
4	
5	A self-hosted platform-as-a-service for hosting non-production applications (demos, experiments) in a dedicated GCP project. Designed for low operator maintenance with strong cost controls and a Heroku-style developer experience.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Table of contents
10	
11	1. [Goals and non-goals](#1-goals-and-non-goals)
12	2. [Personas](#2-personas)
13	3. [Architecture overview](#3-architecture-overview)
14	4. [Security model](#4-security-model)
15	5. [Ownership model](#5-ownership-model)
16	6. [Repo and quota model](#6-repo-and-quota-model)
17	7. [Developer interface](#7-developer-interface)
18	8. [Operator interface](#8-operator-interface)
19	9. [Bootstrap binary](#9-bootstrap-binary)
20	10. [Hibernation](#10-hibernation)
21	11. [Key decisions log](#11-key-decisions-log)
22	12. [Open questions](#12-open-questions)
23	13. [Iterative build plan](#13-iterative-build-plan)
24	
25	---
26	
27	## 1. Goals and non-goals
28	
29	### Goals
30	
31	- Let developers deploy containerised apps with nothing more than a git push
32	- Support HTTP servers, background workers, and scheduled jobs
33	- Provide managed persistence: blob storage, databases, and queues
34	- Enforce cost caps automatically via quota limits; require no manual intervention for routine use
35	- Detect and hibernate idle apps; wake them transparently on next request
36	- Manage DNS and HTTPS automatically under an operator-controlled domain
37	- Keep apps unreachable from the public internet when required
38	- Allow ownership transfer of apps between repos without downtime
39	- Require part-time attention from a single, rotating operator
40	
41	### Non-goals
42	
43	- Production workloads — Morsel has no SLA
44	- Multi-region or high-availability deployments
45	- Workloads requiring GPUs or specialised hardware
46	- Replacing an internal developer portal (Backstage, etc.)
47	- Serving as a general-purpose CI/CD platform
48	- Data backup or disaster recovery — app owners are responsible for data they cannot afford to lose
49	
50	---
51	
52	## 2. Personas
53	
54	### Designer / implementer
55	
56	Builds and evolves the platform itself. Comfortable with Kubernetes internals and GCP. Interacts with the full stack. This role is not the operator; complexity is acceptable here because it is absorbed once during construction and rarely during maintenance.
57	
58	### Operator
59	
60	Manages the running platform on a part-time basis. The role may rotate. The operator has no expectation of Kubernetes or GCP knowledge. Their entire workflow is through two tools: the `morsel` CLI (for installation, upgrades, and access management) and a purpose-built admin UI (for day-to-day management). Routine tasks should take minutes, not hours.
61	
62	The operator's task surface is deliberately narrow:
63	
64	- Run `morsel service bootstrap` to install or upgrade the platform
65	- Review new repos that have auto-registered
66	- Promote repos to higher quota tiers on request
67	- Transfer app ownership in unusual circumstances
68	- Periodically review and clean up apps from deleted or archived repos
69	- Glance at cost and health dashboards
70	- Act on alerts (failed deploys, expiring certs)
71	
72	### Developer / app owner
73	
74	A member of the GitHub organisation. Deploys and operates apps on behalf of their team. No cloud or Kubernetes knowledge required. Their entire interface is a git repository and `*.morsel.json` files in the `.morsel/` folder.
75	
76	---
77	
78	## 3. Architecture overview
79	
80	Morsel is built on GKE running in a dedicated non-production GCP project. Kubernetes complexity is fully hidden from operators and developers; only the designer interacts with it directly.
81	
82	| Layer | Responsibility |
83	|---|---|
84	| Developer experience | `git push` triggers GitHub Actions: build container, push to staging registry, call Morsel deploy API |
85	| Control plane | Morsel API (manifest apply, hibernation, certificate management, DNS management) |
86	| GKE runtime | One namespace per app; Deployments, CronJobs, ResourceQuotas, LimitRanges |
87	| Persistence | Blob service (`blob.morsel.internal`), queue service (`queue.morsel.internal`), shared in-cluster Postgres — all backed by in-cluster storage. Morsel API state in SQLite. |
88	| Network / DNS / TLS | GKE Gateway API, VPC-native, internal load balancer, Cloud DNS or Cloudflare, Let's Encrypt (managed by Morsel API) |
89	| Identity / cost | GitHub OIDC tokens, Workload Identity Federation (via Platform abstraction), GCP Budgets (informational), Namespace ResourceQuota |
90	
91	---
92	
93	## 4. Security model
94	
95	Morsel is a convenience service. It must not create security liability for the operator's wider organisation. The decisions in this section are non-negotiable: they exist specifically to ensure that a compromised or misbehaving Morsel cannot be used as a stepping stone into the operator's broader infrastructure.
96	
97	### Core principle: GitHub calls Morsel, not the other way around
98	
99	GitHub Actions calls the Morsel API and presents a short-lived OIDC token as proof of identity. Morsel never holds a GitHub credential of any kind.
100	
101	### GitHub OIDC token flow
102	
103	1. GitHub Actions generates a short-lived JWT (5-minute TTL) signed by GitHub's private key
104	2. The token contains verifiable claims: repository, git ref, and workflow SHA
105	3. Morsel validates the token signature against GitHub's public JWKS endpoint (read-only, no credential required)
106	4. Morsel extracts the `repository` claim and uses it as the app owner identity
107	
108	### What Morsel holds vs. never holds
109	
110	| Morsel holds | Morsel never holds |
111	|---|---|
112	| GitHub's public JWKS URL (read-only) | GitHub PAT or OAuth token |
113	| Its own internal repo and app records | Org membership read access |
114	| GCP service account credentials (via Workload Identity) | Any credential that can enumerate the GitHub org |
115	
116	### Blast radius if Morsel is compromised
117	
118	An attacker who fully compromises Morsel can: deploy or delete apps on the platform, exhaust quota, and access data in platform-managed persistence.
119	
120	They cannot: enumerate the GitHub organisation, read source code, impersonate users outside the platform, or touch any GCP project other than the dedicated Morsel project.
121	
122	This blast radius must be preserved. Any future change that would expand it — for example, granting Morsel's service account permissions in another GCP project — requires explicit designer sign-off and a documented rationale in this spec.
123	
124	### GCP project isolation
125	
126	Morsel runs in a dedicated GCP project. This is a hard isolation boundary, not a convention.
127	
128	- All Morsel resources (GKE cluster, Artifact Registry, GCS, in-cluster Postgres) live in this project and nowhere else
129	- The one exception is a Cloudflare API token if Cloudflare is selected as the DNS provider — see DNS provider section below
130	- Morsel's GCP service accounts are granted no roles outside this project
131	- No service account key files are created; all GCP authentication uses Workload Identity
132	- The project has no shared VPC peering or org-level service account bindings that would allow lateral movement to other GCP projects
133	
134	The dedicated project means that even with full GCP control-plane access to the Morsel project, an attacker cannot affect the operator's other projects.
135	
136	### IAM least-privilege policy
137	
138	Morsel's service accounts are granted the minimum roles required and nothing broader.
139	
140	| Service account | Permitted roles | Scope |
141	|---|---|---|
142	| Morsel API | `artifactregistry.writer` (staging + canonical repo) | Morsel project only |
143	| GKE node pool | `artifactregistry.reader` (canonical repo) | Morsel project only |
144	| GitHub Actions (via WIF) | `artifactregistry.writer` (staging repo only) | Morsel project only |
145	
146	No service account is granted any Editor, Owner, or project-level primitive role. All IAM is managed by the bootstrap binary and codified in the binary's provisioning logic — no ad-hoc console changes.
147	
148	### Artifact Registry: staging handshake
149	
150	Container images are stored in a single private Artifact Registry repository. Push isolation between repos is enforced by the Morsel API, not by registry ACLs. No GitHub Actions workflow ever has write access to the canonical image store.
151	
152	**The staging handshake:**
153	
154	1. GitHub Actions builds the image and pushes it to a short-lived staging repository. GitHub Actions has write access to the staging repository only.
155	2. GitHub Actions calls the Morsel deploy API with the image digest and OIDC token.
156	3. Morsel validates the token, confirms the repo claim matches the app's registered repo, then performs a registry-side copy from staging into the canonical repository under a path it controls (`repo-slug/app-name`). This is a metadata operation — no image data travels over the network.
157	4. Morsel records the new digest as `current` and the previous digest as `last-healthy` in its own database.
158	5. Morsel deletes the staging image.
159	6. Morsel API applies the updated Kubernetes manifest directly via client-go.
160	
161	**Rollback:** If a deploy fails health checks, Morsel redeploys the `last-healthy` digest without any registry interaction. Only two digests per app are retained in the canonical repository. The staging repository has a 1-hour TTL cleanup policy as a safety net against abandoned pushes.
162	
163	### Credential summary: nothing stored, nothing long-lived
164	
165	| Credential relationship | Mechanism | Stored secret? |
166	|---|---|---|
167	| GitHub Actions → GCP (staging registry push) | Workload Identity Federation + OIDC | No |
168	| GitHub Actions → Morsel API | GitHub OIDC JWT (5-min TTL) | No |
169	| Morsel API → Artifact Registry | Workload Identity (ambient GKE service account) | No |
170	| Morsel API → GCS | Workload Identity (ambient GKE service account) | No |
171	| GKE nodes → Artifact Registry | Node pool service account (ambient GCP identity) | No |
172	
173	No long-lived credential exists anywhere in the system. There is nothing to rotate, nothing to leak, and nothing stored in GitHub Actions secrets or Kubernetes Secrets for platform-level access.
174	
175	### Network: Private Google Access
176	
177	All traffic between GKE and GCP managed services (Artifact Registry, GCS, Cloud DNS) is routed via Private Google Access — Google's internal network, not the public internet. No GCP API endpoint needs to be reachable from the internet for the platform to function.
178	
179	GitHub Actions workflows run on GitHub-hosted runners and therefore do make outbound connections to GCP over the internet (to exchange the OIDC token and push to the staging registry). This is accepted: the connection is outbound-only, TLS-secured, and authenticated by a short-lived cryptographically signed token. No inbound internet access to any Morsel resource is required for this flow.
180	
181	### Self-hosted runners: explicitly out of scope
182	
183	Running self-hosted GitHub Actions runners inside the VPC would eliminate the internet leg of the GitHub Actions → GCP connection but would introduce persistent VMs requiring patching, scaling, and lifecycle management. This operational cost is not justified for a non-production convenience platform. This decision is recorded here so it is not revisited without deliberate consideration.
184	
185	### DNS provider: Cloud DNS or Cloudflare
186	
187	Morsel supports two DNS providers. The operator selects one when answering `GCPPlatform` bootstrap prompts.
188	
189	**Cloud DNS:** DNS is managed entirely within the Morsel GCP project. No credentials required — the Morsel API authenticates via its ambient Workload Identity. All secrets remain within the GCP project boundary.
190	
191	**Cloudflare:** The Morsel API is configured with a Cloudflare API token stored as a Secret Manager secret. This is the one case where a Morsel secret has reach outside the GCP project boundary — the token can modify DNS records for the configured zone. The token must be scoped as tightly as Cloudflare's token model allows: edit access to a single zone, no other permissions. The bootstrap wizard enforces this by generating the token scope instructions and validating the token's permissions before proceeding.
192	
193	---
194	
195	## 5. Ownership model
196	
197	### Repos as owners
198	
199	Apps belong to the GitHub repository they are deployed from. The repo is the stable, unambiguous identity that Morsel can verify directly from the OIDC token — which contains the `repository` claim as a standard field — without any GitHub API calls.
200	
201	Anyone who can trigger a GitHub Actions workflow on a repo can deploy that repo's apps. No other ownership concept exists in Morsel.
202	
203	### First deploy and auto-registration
204	
205	When Morsel receives the first deploy from a previously unknown repo, it automatically creates a repo record, assigns the default quota tier, and registers the app. The deploy succeeds immediately. The operator receives a digest notification but is not in the critical path.
206	
207	### Ownership in the Morsel token
208	
209	When a GitHub OIDC token is exchanged for a Morsel token, the `repository` claim is encoded directly:
210	
211	```json
212	{
213	  "sub": "repo:org/my-repo",
214	  "repo": "org/my-repo",
215	  "role": "developer",
216	  "exp": 1234567890
217	}
218	```
219	
220	Developers can only read or modify apps belonging to their repo. Any attempt to access another repo's apps returns 403.
221	
222	### Ownership lifecycle
223	
224	| Event | Platform behaviour |
225	|---|---|
226	| New contributor gains repo access | Automatically gains deploy access on next workflow run. No operator action. |
227	| Contributor loses repo access | Access revoked on next OIDC token validation. Apps remain under repo ownership. |
228	| Repo transferred to another org/team in GitHub | New owners deploy; Morsel updates ownership on next successful deploy. |
229	| Repo deleted or archived in GitHub | App becomes orphaned. Morsel has no mechanism to detect this automatically — see orphaned apps below. |
230	| Unusual circumstance | Operator can transfer app ownership directly via admin UI. |
231	
232	### Orphaned apps
233	
234	An app is orphaned when its GitHub repo has been deleted or archived. Morsel has no way to detect this condition automatically — it holds no GitHub token and receives no GitHub webhook events. Orphaned apps will continue running and consuming resources until the operator identifies and removes them.
235	
236	Detecting orphaned apps is an open problem. The operator is the only current mechanism — periodic manual review of the stale apps list in the admin UI (sorted by last deploy date) is the recommended approach until an automated detection mechanism is designed.
237	
238	---
239	
240	## 6. Repo and quota model
241	
242	### Automatic repo onboarding
243	
244	When Morsel receives the first deploy request from a previously unknown repo, it automatically creates a repo record and assigns the default quota tier. The deploy succeeds immediately. The operator receives a digest notification but is not in the critical path.
245	
246	This achieves low-maintenance onboarding while bounding cost exposure through the default tier limits.
247	
248	### Quota tiers
249	
250	Quota is tracked per repo. Cost attribution, app limits, and tier promotion all attach to the repo identity.
251	
252	| Attribute | Default tier | Standard tier | Power tier | Notes |
253	|---|---|---|---|---|
254	| Assignment | Automatic | Operator assigned | Operator assigned | Default on first deploy |
255	| Max apps | 2 | 10 | 25 | Per repo |
256	| CPU per app | 0.5 cores | 1 core | 4 cores | Kubernetes limit |
257	| Memory per app | 512 MB | 1 GB | 4 GB | Kubernetes limit |
258	| Blob storage per app | 1 GB | 10 GB | 50 GB | Enforced by blob service |
259	| Database storage per app | 5 GB | 20 GB | 100 GB | Advisory limit — enforced by Morsel, not by Postgres |
260	| Queue storage per app | 1 GB | 10 GB | 50 GB | Enforced by queue service — enqueue rejected when exceeded |
261	| Hibernate after | 24 hrs idle | 48 hrs idle | 72 hrs idle | Configurable per app |
262	
263	The default tier is intentionally sized so that a repo can validate a working application without hitting constraints, but cannot consume meaningful budget without the operator becoming aware.
264	
265	### Quota enforcement
266	
267	- Kubernetes `ResourceQuota` and `LimitRange` enforce CPU and memory at the namespace level
268	- When a repo hits its app count limit, the deploy API returns a clear error directing developers to contact the operator
269	- When a repo hits its tier ceiling, deploys requesting additional resources are rejected with a clear error. App owners contact the operator to request a tier upgrade.
270	- Operator can promote a repo's tier in the admin UI in under 30 seconds
271	
272	---
273	
274	## 7. Developer interface
275	
276	### *.morsel.json
277	
278	The entire configuration surface for a developer is one or more `*.morsel.json` files in the `.morsel/` folder of their repository. No Kubernetes knowledge required.
279	
280	```json
281	{
282	  "name": "my-demo-app",
283	  "type": "http",
284	  "schedule": "0 9 * * 1-5",
285	  "tier": "small",
286	  "private": true,
287	  "idle_after": "24h",
288	  "health_check": {
289	    "liveness_path": "/livez",
290	    "readiness_path": "/healthz",
291	    "timeout": "60s",
292	    "interval": "5s",
293	    "threshold": 3
294	  },
295	  "timeout": "1h",
296	  "retries": 0,
297	  "persistence": {
298	    "database": { "permanent": true },
299	    "storage": { "permanent": false },
300	    "queues": { "permanent": false }
301	  }
302	}
303	```
304	
305	| Field | Values | Notes |
306	|---|---|---|
307	| `name` | string | Unique within the repo. Named apps get `name.repo.apps.example.com`; unnamed apps get `repo.apps.example.com`. |
308	| `type` | `http` \| `worker` \| `cronjob` | Determines the Kubernetes workload type. |
309	| `schedule` | cron expression | Required when `type` is `cronjob`. |
310	| `tier` | `small` \| `medium` \| `large` | Resource size within the repo's quota tier. |
311	| `private` | boolean | `true` for internal-only ingress; `false` for public. |
312	| `idle_after` | duration string | Idle threshold before hibernation. Overrides platform default. e.g. `"24h"`, `"48h"`. |
313	| `health_check.liveness_path` | URL path string | Kubernetes liveness probe path. Default `/livez`. HTTP apps only. Omit `health_check` block entirely to disable probes. |
314	| `health_check.readiness_path` | URL path string | Kubernetes readiness probe path. Default `/healthz`. HTTP apps only. |
315	| `health_check.timeout` | duration string | Time to wait for health check to pass after deploy. Default `"60s"`. |
316	| `health_check.interval` | duration string | Time between probe attempts. Default `"5s"`. |
317	| `health_check.threshold` | integer | Consecutive successes required to mark healthy. Default `3`. |
318	| `timeout` | duration string | Maximum run duration for CronJobs. Required when `type` is `cronjob`. |
319	| `retries` | integer | Retry count on failure for CronJobs. Default `0`. |
320	| `persistence.database` | `{ permanent }` or omit | Provisions a Postgres database on the shared cluster instance. App connects via `database.morsel.internal`. `permanent`: boolean, default `false`. |
321	| `persistence.storage` | `{ permanent }` or `true` / omit | Provisions blob storage quota. `permanent`: boolean, default `false`. App accesses via `blob.morsel.internal`. |
322	| `persistence.queues` | `{ permanent }` or `true` / omit | Enables queue service access. App creates queues at runtime via `queue.morsel.internal`. `permanent`: boolean, default `false`. Quota applies to total storage across all app queues. |
323	
324	### Deploy flow
325	
326	Each app must have a `Dockerfile` at the repository root. The build context is the repository root.
327	
328	1. Developer pushes to the default branch
329	2. GitHub Actions discovers all `*.morsel.json` files in `.morsel/`
330	3. Workflow calls `POST /api/repos/:slug/sync` with full list of declared app names and git context
331	4. Morsel diffs against its records; handles deletions respecting permanent resource flags per resource type
332	5. Workflow fans out parallel matrix jobs — one per app: build container, push to staging registry
333	6. Each job calls `POST /api/repos/:slug/apps` with image digest, git ref, git SHA, and Morsel token
334	7. Morsel validates token, copies image from staging to canonical registry, updates manifest via client-go
335	8. App passes health checks → deploy confirmed. Failure → Morsel automatically redeploys last-healthy digest
336

339	## 8. Operator interface
340	
341	The operator interacts with Morsel through exactly two tools: the `morsel` CLI (covered in section 9) and a web admin UI. No terminal, kubectl, GCP console, or cloud knowledge is required for any routine operation.

345	| Area | Actions |

348	| Repo management | View all repos; per-repo app count, cost, and tier; promote/demote quota tier |
349	| Approvals | View pending approvals across all repos; batch approve, reject, or ignore per app |
350	| Stale apps | List apps sorted by last deploy date; identify and clean up apps from deleted or archived repos |
351	| Cost and quotas | Total and per-repo spend; budget ceiling (informational); apps approaching quota ceiling; hibernate candidates |
352	| Platform status | Cluster status summary; failed deploy log; cert and DNS alerts; upgrade notifications |

359	- **Periodically:** review and batch action pending approvals

365	
366	## 9. `morsel` CLI
367	
368	The `morsel` binary is the operator's sole interface for installing, configuring, and upgrading the platform. It has no external dependencies — no Terraform, no gcloud, no kubectl. The operator needs only a browser and the binary itself.
369	
370	### Distribution
371	
372	Released as a static Go binary via GitHub Releases. The operator downloads the binary for their platform (Linux/macOS/Windows) and runs it directly. No package manager or installer required.
373	
374	```
375	curl -L https://github.com/org/morsel/releases/latest/download/morsel-$(uname -s)-$(uname -m) \
376	  -o morsel && chmod +x morsel
377	./morsel service bootstrap
378	```
379	
380	### Implementation: no external tool dependencies
381	
382	All provisioning is implemented directly in Go using embedded libraries. The operator's machine needs nothing installed beyond the binary itself.
383	
384	| Concern | Implementation |
385	|---|---|
386	| GCP resource provisioning | GCP Go SDK (`cloud.google.com/go`) — compiled into binary |
387	| Kubernetes resource management | `k8s.io/client-go` — compiled into binary |
388	| GCP authentication | OAuth2 Go library + localhost callback — compiled into binary |
389	
390	This means the binary is self-contained and its behaviour is fully deterministic. There is no external tool version mismatch to debug.
391	
392	### Subcommands
393	
394	### CLI structure
395	
396	`morsel service` is the entry point for all operator-facing platform management.
397	
398	```
399	morsel [--profile <name>] service bootstrap [--platform <name>]
400	morsel [--profile <name>] service status
401	morsel [--profile <name>] service login
402	morsel [--profile <name>] service logout
403	morsel [--profile <name>] service delete
404	morsel [--profile <name>] service upgrade retry
405	
406	morsel [--profile <name>] service operator add --principal morsel-operators@example.com
407	morsel [--profile <name>] service operator remove --principal alice@example.com
408	morsel [--profile <name>] service operator list
409	
410	morsel [--profile <name>] lint
411	morsel [--profile <name>] lint --staged
412	morsel [--profile <name>] lint --fix
413	
414	morsel [--profile <name>] app deploy   # local platform profiles only
415	```
416	
417	`--profile` defaults to `default`. Each profile maps to `~/.config/morsel/<profile>.profile.json`.
418	
419	| Command | Purpose |
420	|---|---|
421	| Flag | `--profile <name>` | Selects the active profile. Defaults to `default`. Applies to all subcommands. |
422	| `morsel service login` | Authenticates to the Morsel instance. Triggers GCP OAuth browser flow. Writes profile to disk on success. |
423	| `morsel service logout` | Revokes refresh token server-side. Deletes profile file. |
424	| `morsel service bootstrap` | Installs or upgrades the platform. Triggers login flow if no valid profile exists. |
425	| `morsel service status` | Reports the health of all platform components without making any changes. |
426	| `morsel service delete` | Tears down all platform resources. Requires explicit confirmation. Intended for designer use only. |
427	| `morsel service upgrade retry` | Retries app redeployments that failed during the most recent platform upgrade. |
428	| `morsel service operator add` | Grants admin UI access to a Google account or Google Group. |
429	| `morsel service operator remove` | Revokes admin UI access from a principal. |
430	| `morsel service operator list` | Lists all principals currently granted admin UI access. |
431	| `morsel lint` | Validates all `*.morsel.json` files in `.morsel/`. |
432	| `morsel lint --staged` | Validates only git-staged `*.morsel.json` files. Pre-commit hook use. |
433	| `morsel lint --fix` | Auto-remediates safe issues. |
434	| `morsel app deploy` | Deploys all apps in `.morsel/`. Works in local development and GitHub Actions CI. Platform-agnostic — `Platform.DeployCredentials()` handles all credential and registry differences. Uses staging handshake on cloud platforms; pushes directly to canonical registry on local platform. |
435	
436	### Configuration storage
437	
438	Wizard configuration is stored as a secret in Secret Manager (`morsel-bootstrap-config`) alongside Morsel's other platform secrets. This means:
439	
440	- Platform configuration is not tied to the operator's local machine
441	- Any operator (the role rotates) can run `morsel service bootstrap` on any machine and it reads existing configuration automatically
442	- On first run, configuration is held in memory through provisioning and written to Secret Manager once it is available
443	- On subsequent runs, configuration is read from Secret Manager before any other action
444	
445	Per-operator authentication state (tokens, GCP project, region, API URL) is stored locally in `~/.config/morsel/<profile>.profile.json` with `0600` permissions. This file is only created on successful authentication.
446	
447	### Install flow
448	
449	`morsel service bootstrap` runs four phases in sequence. Each phase is fully idempotent — if the binary is interrupted and rerun, it continues from where it left off without duplicating resources.
450	
451	#### Phase 1 — GCP authentication
452	
453	The binary opens the system browser to a GCP OAuth consent screen. The operator logs in with their Google account. The OAuth token is returned to a localhost callback listener in the binary. The token is used only for the duration of the run; it is not persisted to disk.
454	
455	The binary requests the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform` scope, bounded to the nominated project. This is a broad scope, but it is required to create GCP resources. It is held only in memory and for the duration of the session.
456	
457	#### Phase 2 — Preflight checks
458	
459	Before provisioning, the platform validates that prerequisites are met. For `GCPPlatform` these checks run after the OAuth flow and before any resources are created. All checks must pass before proceeding. Failures print a specific, actionable error message and exit cleanly.
460	
461	| Check | Failure message | Notes |
462	|---|---|---|
463	| Billing active | "Billing is not enabled on project {id}. Enable it at console.cloud.google.com/billing." | |
464	| Required APIs enabled | "The following APIs must be enabled: {list}. Run: gcloud services enable {list} --project {id}" | |
465	| Operator IAM permissions | "Your account is missing the following roles: {list}. Ask a project owner to grant them." | |
466	| GKE quota sufficient | "Insufficient CPU/node quota in region {region}. Request a quota increase at console.cloud.google.com/iam-admin/quotas." | |
467	| Cloud DNS zone exists | "No Cloud DNS zone found for {domain}. Create one first or use a different domain." | Cloud DNS provider only |
468	
469	#### Phase 3 — Wizard
470	
471	The wizard runs on first invocation only, when no bootstrap config exists in Secret Manager. It collects the minimum configuration that cannot be defaulted. Everything else can be changed later in the admin UI.
472	
473	| Prompt | Default | Notes |
474	|---|---|---|
475	These are examples of what `GCPPlatform.BootstrapPrompts()` returns. The actual prompts are defined by the platform implementation, not the wizard.
476	
477	| Prompt | Default | Notes |
478	|---|---|---|
479	| GCP project ID | Detected from OAuth token | Operator confirms or overrides |
480	| GCP region | `us-central1` | Detected from project defaults if set |
481	| Base domain | None — required | Validated against Cloud DNS or Cloudflare |
482	| GitHub org slug | None — required | Used to scope OIDC token validation |
483	| Notification email | None — required | Stored in Secret Manager |
484	| Monthly budget ceiling | `$500` | Informational — shown in cost dashboard |
485	| DNS provider | `Cloud DNS` | `Cloud DNS` or `Cloudflare` |
486	| Operator access | None — required | Google account or Group email |
487	
488	After the wizard, the binary prints a full summary of what will be created and an estimated monthly cost at typical utilisation, then asks for confirmation before proceeding.
489	
490	#### Phase 4 — Provisioning
491	
492	Resources are created in dependency order. The operator sees friendly progress output; raw API responses are written to a log file for debugging if needed.
493	
494	```
495	✓ State bucket created
496	✓ VPC and Private Google Access configured
497	  Creating GKE cluster… (this takes 4–6 minutes)
498	✓ GKE cluster ready
499	✓ Artifact Registry (staging + canonical repositories)
500	✓ Workload Identity Federation configured
501	✓ IAM bindings applied
502	✓ Secret Manager provisioned
503	✓ Morsel API installed
504	✓ Morsel admin UI installed
505	✓ Identity-Aware Proxy configured
506	✓ Operator access granted
507	  Waiting for TLS certificate… (up to 2 minutes)
508	✓ TLS certificate issued
509	✓ Smoke test passed
510	
511	Morsel is ready.
512	
513	Admin UI:  https://admin.apps.example.com
514	Access:    Sign in with your Google account (morsel-operators@example.com)
515	```
516	
517	No password is created or stored. Access to the admin UI is controlled entirely by IAP. The operator authenticates with their existing Google account.
518	
519	### Subsequent runs: upgrades
520	
521	On any run where a bootstrap config exists in Secret Manager, `morsel service bootstrap` skips the wizard, reads existing config, prints a summary of what will change, asks for confirmation, then applies changes in dependency order. Upgrades are rolling — the platform remains operational throughout.
522	
523	The designer controls what each binary version upgrades to by embedding target versions of all dependencies (GKE release channel, Morsel API and UI versions) at compile time. The operator never chooses versions; they simply run the current binary.
524	
525	### Idempotency guarantee
526	
527	Every operation performed by the bootstrap binary follows a check-then-act pattern:
528	
529	1. Check whether the resource already exists in its desired state
530	2. If yes, skip and report `✓ (already up to date)`
531	3. If no, create or update, then verify
532	
533	This means `morsel service bootstrap` is safe to run multiple times without side effects.

538	## 10. Authentication and authorisation
539	
540	### Token model
541	
542	Morsel uses a two-token model: a short-lived access token and a long-lived refresh token. All API requests require a valid access token. The access token is a signed JWT verified by signature alone — no database lookup on every request.
543	
544	| Token | Lifetime | Storage | Notes |
545	|---|---|---|---|
546	| Access token | 15 min (operator configurable) | In memory only — never written to disk | JWT; contains identity, role, and repo. Verified by signature. |
547	| Refresh token | 90 days | SQLite (server-side) + `~/.config/morsel/<profile>.profile.json` (client-side) | Opaque token. Exchanged for a new access token. Rotated on every refresh. |
548	
549	The access token TTL is the maximum lag before role changes take effect. No per-request database lookup is required.
550	
551	### Exchange endpoints
552	
553	```
554	POST /api/token/github-oidc    → access token (10 min), no refresh token
555	POST /api/token/gcp-oidc       → access token (15 min) + refresh token (90 days)
556	POST /api/token/refresh        → access token (15 min) + refresh token (90 days, rotated)
557	```
558	
559	GitHub Actions re-exchanges on every workflow run and does not need a refresh token. The 10-minute access token covers typical workflow duration.
560	
561	The GCP OIDC exchange resolves the caller's role at issuance time by checking whether their Google identity matches the operator principal configured at bootstrap. Role is encoded in the token; no directory lookup is needed on subsequent requests.
562	
563	Refresh tokens are rotated on every use — the old token is invalidated and a new one issued. A stolen refresh token can be used at most once before the legitimate user's next refresh invalidates it.
564	
565	### Revocation
566	
567	Revoking a refresh token (e.g. when a developer leaves the org) is a single SQLite delete. The associated access token remains valid until expiry — at most one TTL period (default 15 minutes). No per-request revocation check is needed.
568	
569	### CLI authentication
570	
571	#### Profiles
572	
573	The CLI supports multiple named profiles, each representing a distinct Morsel instance. The active profile is selected with the top-level `--profile` flag, which defaults to `default`.
574	
575	```
576	morsel --profile default service bootstrap
577	morsel --profile data-platform service status
578	morsel --profile dev-tools lint
579	```
580	
581	Each profile is stored as `~/.config/morsel/<profile>.profile.json` with `0600` permissions. The file is only written on successful authentication — never created for failed or incomplete auth flows.
582	
583	Profile file shape:
584	
585	```json
586	{
587	  "project": "morsel-prod",
588	  "region": "us-central1",
589	  "api_url": "https://admin.apps.example.com",
590	  "access_token": "eyJ...",
591	  "access_token_expires_at": "2026-05-26T10:15:00Z",
592	  "refresh_token": "mrl_...",
593	  "refresh_token_expires_at": "2026-08-26T10:00:00Z"
594	}
595	```
596	
597	#### Auth flow on every command invocation
598	
599	1. Load `~/.config/morsel/<profile>.profile.json` — if absent, collect GCP project and region interactively (held in memory only)
600	2. Check `access_token_expires_at` — if valid, proceed
601	3. If expired, attempt silent refresh via `POST /api/token/refresh` — on success write updated tokens to profile
602	4. If refresh token expired or absent, trigger interactive GCP OAuth browser flow — on success write full profile to disk (create or update)
603	5. Execute command
604	
605	Project and region collected before a failed auth are held in memory only for that session. The profile is never written until authentication succeeds.
606	
607	#### Login and logout
608	
609	```
610	morsel service login      # explicit login — triggers OAuth flow, writes profile on success
611	morsel service logout     # revokes refresh token server-side, deletes profile file
612	```
613	
614	`morsel service bootstrap` triggers the login flow automatically if no valid profile exists for the active profile name.
615	
616	#### Transparent token refresh
617	
618	When a request fails with 401, the CLI silently calls `/api/token/refresh`, updates the profile file with the new tokens, and retries the original request. The user never sees it happen.
619	
620	### RBAC
621	
622	Role is determined at token exchange time and encoded in the access token. Two roles exist: operator and developer.
623	
624	| Operation | Developer | Operator |
625	|---|---|---|
626	| Deploy, update own repo's apps | ✓ | ✓ |
627	| Hibernate, wake, delete own repo's apps | ✓ | ✓ |
628	| List and view own repo's apps | ✓ | ✓ |
629	| View own repo's cost and quota | ✓ | ✓ |
630	| Request protected config change | ✓ | ✓ |
631	| View own repo's pending approvals | ✓ | ✓ |
632	| View all repos and apps | ✗ | ✓ |
633	| Batch approve, reject, or ignore approvals | ✗ | ✓ |
634	| Transfer app ownership | ✗ | ✓ |
635	| Promote repo tier | ✗ | ✓ |
636	| Override permanent resource protection | ✗ | ✓ |
637	| Delete apps from archived or deleted repos | ✗ | ✓ |
638	| `morsel service bootstrap` | ✗ | ✓ |
639	
640	Developers are scoped to their own repo's apps. Any attempt to read or modify another repo's app returns 403.
641

644	
645	## 11. App operations
646	
647	All app operations require a valid Morsel access token. Developers are scoped to their own repo — any request where the token's `repo` claim does not match the `:slug` in the URL returns 403. Operators may access any repo.
648	
649	App names are unique within a repo. The repo slug in the URL is the GitHub repo name without the org prefix — `org/my-repo` becomes `my-repo`.
650	
651	### Upsert — create or update
652	
653	Handles both first deploy and subsequent updates. Morsel determines from its own state whether this is a create or update. The caller always sends the full app declaration contents and the image digest.
654	
655	```
656	POST /api/repos/:slug/apps
657	Authorization: Bearer <morsel-token>
658	
659	{
660	  "app": { ...app declaration contents... },
661	  "image": "sha256:abc123",
662	  "git_ref": "refs/heads/main",
663	  "git_sha": "a1b2c3d4"
664	}
665	
666	→ 202 Accepted
667	  Location: /api/repos/my-repo/apps/my-demo-app/operations/op_abc123
668	  Retry-After: 5
669	
670	{
671	  "operation_id": "op_abc123",
672	  "applied": {
673	    "image": "sha256:abc123",
674	    "private": true,
675	    "idle_after": "48h"
676	  },
677	  "pending_approval": {
678	    "tier": {
679	      "id": "apr_abc123",
680	      "current_value": "small",
681	      "requested_value": "medium",
682	      "expires_at": "2026-06-26T10:00:00Z"
683	    }
684	  },
685	  "ignored": {}
686	}
687	```
688	
689	**Protected config** — fields that require operator approval before taking effect:
690	
691	| Field | Reason |
692	|---|---|
693	| `tier` | Affects resource consumption |
694	| Persistence additions beyond current quota | Would exceed approved resource limits |
695	| App count beyond repo limit | Would exceed approved app limit |
696	
697	All other fields are applied immediately on deploy.
698	
699	Destructive persistence changes (removing a declared resource) return 409 unless `?force=true` is passed:
700	
701	```
702	→ 409 Conflict
703	{
704	  "error": "permanent_resource",
705	  "detail": "persistence.database is marked permanent and cannot be removed by a developer",
706	  "remedy": "set permanent to false, deploy, then remove the declaration"
707	}
708	
709	The `?force=true` flag overrides permanent resource protection. It is available to operators only — developers receive 403 if they attempt it.
710	```
711	
712	For the unnamed app case, `name` is omitted from the app declaration and Morsel uses the repo slug as the app name, resulting in the URL `my-repo.apps.example.com`.
713	
714	### Delete single app
715	
716	Stops the app immediately and removes all Kubernetes resources. Persistence enters the operator-configured grace period.
717	
718	```
719	DELETE /api/repos/:slug/apps/:name
720	Authorization: Bearer <morsel-token>
721	
722	→ 200 OK
723	{
724	  "deleted_at": "2026-05-26T10:00:00Z",
725	  "persistence_purge_after": "2026-06-25T10:00:00Z"
726	}
727	```
728	
729	### Delete all apps in a repo
730	
731	Deletes every app belonging to the repo. Persistence for all apps enters the grace period. Intended for repo retirement or cleanup.
732	
733	```

735	Authorization: Bearer <morsel-token>
736	
737	→ 200 OK

739	  "deleted": ["my-demo-app", "worker", "scheduler"],

886	### Sync
887	
888	Called once per workflow run before individual app deploys. Tells Morsel the complete declared set of apps for this repo at this git SHA. Morsel diffs against its own records and deletes any app no longer declared, subject to permanent resource rules.
889	
890	Apps with only non-permanent persistence enter the grace period immediately. Apps with permanent persistence have their Kubernetes resources removed but permanent resources are retained until an operator explicitly removes them with `?force=true`.
891	
892	```
893	POST /api/repos/:slug/sync
894	Authorization: Bearer <morsel-token>
895	
896	{

1239	## 14. Runtime services
1240	
1241	Morsel provides a set of runtime services available to all apps within the platform. Apps access these services via fixed internal hostnames within the VPC. No GCP credentials, SDK configuration, or service discovery is required from the app.
1242	
1243	### Identity
1244	
1245	Each app runs with its own Kubernetes service account. Internal Morsel services identify callers by their pod's service account — no credentials are passed by the app, and none are visible to the developer.
1246	
1247	### Blob storage — `blob.morsel.internal`
1248	
1249	A lightweight object storage API backed by a GCS bucket. Apps interact with a simple fixed-host HTTP API and have no knowledge of or access to GCS directly.
1250	
1251	**Endpoint:**
1252	```
1253	http://blob.morsel.internal
1254	```
1255	
1256	**API:**
1257	```
1258	GET  /objects/{key}                              # retrieve object
1259	PUT  /objects/{key}                              # store object
1260	GET  /objects?prefix={prefix}&cursor={cursor}    # list keys with optional filter and pagination
1261	```
1262	
1263	**Namespace isolation:** Each app's objects are stored under a namespace prefix derived from the app's pod identity (`repo-slug/app-name/{key}`). The prefix is injected transparently by the blob service — the app uses bare keys only and cannot access another app's objects.
1264	
1265	**Quota enforcement:** The blob service tracks byte usage per app. `PUT` requests that would exceed the app's blob storage allocation return:
1266	
1267	```
1268	429 Too Many Requests
1269	{
1270	  "error": "blob_quota_exceeded",
1271	  "used_bytes": 1073741824,
1272	  "limit_bytes": 1073741824,
1273	  "remedy": "request a storage increase from your platform operator"
1274	}
1275	```
1276	
1277	**Implementation:** The blob service is a small Go service running as a Deployment in the cluster. It authenticates to GCS via its own Workload Identity. Usage tracking is stored in a SQLite file on a Persistent Volume. Quota limits are pushed to the blob service by the Morsel API when an app is provisioned or its tier changes.
1278	
1279	### Database — `database.morsel.internal`
1280	
1281	Apps that declare a database are provisioned a dedicated Postgres database on a shared in-cluster Postgres instance. A PGBouncer sidecar runs alongside the app pod as a connection proxy.
1282	
1283	The app connects using fixed constants — no configuration, no credential management:
1284	
1285	| Constant | Value |
1286	|---|---|
1287	| Host | `database.morsel.internal` |
1288	| Port | `5432` |
1289	| Database | `morsel` |
1290	| Username | `morsel` |
1291	| Password | `morsel` |
1292	
1293	**Isolation:** The constants the developer sees are a PGBouncer convention, not real Postgres credentials. Under the hood PGBouncer authenticates to the shared Postgres instance using a per-app generated credential stored in a Kubernetes Secret scoped to the app's namespace. Each app's Postgres user is granted access only to its own database — cross-app database access is not possible regardless of what the app attempts.
1294	
1295	```
1296	App container → database.morsel.internal:5432 → PGBouncer sidecar (per-app credential from K8s Secret)
1297	                                         ↓
1298	                               Shared Postgres → app's own database only
1299	```
1300	
1301	A developer who execs into their pod and connects directly to `database.morsel.internal:5432` is still routed through their app's PGBouncer and cannot reach another app's sidecar — Kubernetes NetworkPolicy prevents pod-to-pod localhost access.
1302	
1303	**Provisioning:** When an app declares a database, Morsel creates:
1304	- A Postgres database named `{repo-slug}-{app-name}`
1305	- A Postgres user named `{repo-slug}-{app-name}` with a generated password
1306	- A `GRANT ALL` scoped to that database only
1307	- A Kubernetes Secret in the app's namespace containing the real credentials
1308	- A PGBouncer sidecar configuration that maps `morsel/morsel/morsel` to the real credentials
1309	
1310	**Database storage quota** is advisory — Morsel tracks declared storage allocations and blocks tier-exceeding requests, but per-database enforcement at the Postgres level is not possible on a shared instance.
1311	
1312	### Queue — `queue.morsel.internal`
1313	
1314	Apps that declare `persistence.queues` can create and manage queues at runtime via a fixed internal host. No queue names are declared in advance — the app creates queues on demand. Morsel provisions access and enforces a storage quota across all of the app's queues combined.
1315	
1316	**Endpoint:**
1317	```
1318	http://queue.morsel.internal
1319	```
1320	
1321	**API:**
1322	```
1323	PUT    /queues/{name}                 # create queue (idempotent)
1324	DELETE /queues/{name}                 # delete queue and all its messages
1325	GET    /queues                        # list app's queues
1326	POST   /queues/{name}/messages        # enqueue a message
1327	GET    /queues/{name}/messages/next   # dequeue next message (brief poll if empty)
1328	DELETE /queues/{name}/messages/{id}   # acknowledge and remove message
1329	GET    /queues/{name}/depth           # count of pending messages
1330	```
1331	
1332	**Namespace isolation:** Queue names are scoped to the calling app via pod identity. Two apps can use the same queue name without collision — the queue service namespaces all operations by app identity transparently.
1333	
1334	**Quota enforcement:** The queue service tracks total message storage across all of the app's queues. Enqueue requests that would exceed the quota return:
1335	
1336	```
1337	429 Too Many Requests
1338	{
1339	  "error": "queue_quota_exceeded",
1340	  "used_bytes": 1073741824,
1341	  "limit_bytes": 1073741824,
1342	  "remedy": "request a queue storage increase from your platform operator"
1343	}
1344	```
1345	
1346	**Permanence:** Applies to the queues resource as a whole. If `permanent: false`, all queues and messages are deleted after the grace period when the app is removed. If `permanent: true`, the queue service retains them until an operator explicitly removes them.
1347	
1348	**Implementation:** The queue service is a small Go service running as a Deployment in the cluster. Each queue is a Postgres table in the shared instance. The queue service handles all table creation and deletion — the app only interacts with the HTTP API.
1349	
1350	**Worker hibernation:** The Morsel API watcher polls `GET /queues` across all of an app's queues. A worker hibernates when all queues report `idle: true`. The `idle` flag accounts for self-consuming queues — a queue where 100% of the last N messages (platform-configurable, default 100) were produced by the same app consuming them is marked `idle: true` regardless of depth.
1351	
1352	```json
1353	{
1354	  "queues": [
1355	    { "name": "jobs",          "depth": 14, "idle": false },
1356	    { "name": "internal-loop", "depth": 47, "idle": true  }
1357	  ]
1358	}
1359	```
1360	
1361	**Topic semantics (fan-out) are not supported.** Each message is delivered once to one consumer. Apps requiring pub/sub fan-out should deploy a broker as a Morsel app.
1362	
1363	### App-to-app communication
1364	
1365	Apps communicate with each other via their public HTTPS URLs. There is no private inter-app communication channel — apps are peers on the public internet (or within the VPC for private apps).
1366	
1367	A hibernated app wakes transparently on an inbound request from another app, subject to normal cold start latency.
1368	
1369	**Private apps as internal services:** An app with `private: true` is reachable only from within the VPC. Since all Morsel apps run within the same VPC, a private app is effectively an internal service accessible to other Morsel apps but not to the public internet. This is the intended pattern for internal APIs, workers that expose status endpoints, and shared services within a repo.
1370	
1371	**URL convention:**
1372	```
1373	Named app:    https://{app-name}.{repo-slug}.apps.example.com
1374	Unnamed app:  https://{repo-slug}.apps.example.com
1375	```
1376	
1377	### Health checks
1378	
1379	Morsel configures standard Kubernetes liveness and readiness probes for HTTP apps. No custom probe logic is added on top of Kubernetes behaviour.
1380	
1381	| Probe | Kubernetes type | Default path | Behaviour |
1382	|---|---|---|---|
1383	| Liveness | `livenessProbe` | `/livez` | Kubernetes restarts pod if probe fails |
1384	| Readiness | `readinessProbe` | `/healthz` | Kubernetes removes pod from service endpoints until probe passes |
1385	
1386	Both paths are overridable via `health_check.liveness_path` and `health_check.readiness_path` in `morsel.json`. Omitting the `health_check` block entirely disables probes — the pod is considered ready immediately.
1387	
1388	Deploy success is determined by Kubernetes rollout status. Morsel watches the rollout via `client-go` and reports success when the desired number of pods are ready, or failure if the rollout does not complete within the configured timeout.
1389	
1390	Workers and CronJobs have no HTTP health check. Workers are healthy when the process is running. CronJobs are healthy when they exit with code 0 within the configured timeout.
1391	
1392	### CronJob behaviour
1393	
1394	| Property | Behaviour |
1395	|---|---|
1396	| Schedule | Standard cron expression in `morsel.json` |
1397	| Success | Exit code 0 within configured `timeout` |
1398	| Failure | Non-zero exit code or timeout exceeded |
1399	| Default retries | `0` — fail fast, surface problem immediately |
1400	| Retry configuration | `retries` field in `morsel.json` — developer opts in explicitly |
1401	| Failure surfacing | Exit code and stderr captured; visible in deploy history endpoint |
1402	| Hibernation | CronJob suspended when app is hibernated; schedule resumes on wake |
1403	| Timeout mapping | `timeout` maps to Kubernetes Job `activeDeadlineSeconds` |
1404	
1405	### What Morsel does not provide
1406	
1407	| Concern | Expectation |
1408	|---|---|
1409	| Caching (Redis, Memcached) | Developer provisions and manages their own |
1410	| App secrets | Developer manages their own — environment variables or a secrets manager of their choice |
1411	| Service discovery or registry | Apps use fixed URLs; no registry needed |
1412	| Pub/Sub fan-out / topic semantics | Deploy a broker as a Morsel app if needed |
1413

1417	## 15. Error handling
1418	
1419	### Structured error responses
1420	
1421	All Morsel API errors return a consistent JSON structure. Error formatting is the responsibility of the client — the API provides structured data, not pre-formatted messages.
1422	
1423	```json
1424	{
1425	  "error": {
1426	    "code": "quota_exceeded",
1427	    "message": "repo org/my-repo has reached its app limit (2/2) on the default tier",
1428	    "remedy": "contact your platform operator to request a tier upgrade",
1429	    "context": {
1430	      "repo": "org/my-repo",
1431	      "current": 2,
1432	      "limit": 2,
1433	      "tier": "default"
1434	    }
1435	  }
1436	}
1437	```
1438	
1439	Every error carries:
1440	
1441	| Field | Description |
1442	|---|---|
1443	| `code` | Machine-readable stable identifier. Clients branch on this for formatting. |
1444	| `message` | Human-readable description of what went wrong. |
1445	| `remedy` | What the developer should do next. Always present. |
1446	| `context` | Structured data specific to the error type. Present when it helps the client render a better message. |
1447	
1448	### Error codes
1449	
1450	| Code | HTTP status | Scenario |
1451	|---|---|---|
1452	| `quota_exceeded` | 409 | App count, CPU, memory, blob, database, or queue storage limit reached |
1453	| `permanent_resource` | 409 | Attempt to remove a resource marked permanent |
1454	| `invalid_token` | 401 | OIDC or Morsel token invalid or expired |
1455	| `repo_mismatch` | 403 | Token repo claim does not match app's registered repo |
1456	| `image_not_found` | 422 | Image digest not found in staging registry |
1457	| `deploy_failed` | 422 | Kubernetes rollout did not complete — health checks did not pass within timeout |
1458	| `immutable_field` | 422 | Attempt to change a field that cannot be changed after bootstrap |
1459	| `tier_demotion_conflict` | 409 | Demotion would put repo over new tier's limits |
1460	| `platform_unavailable` | 503 | Morsel API cannot reach a required platform service |
1461	
1462	`approval_required` is not an error — protected config changes return 202 Accepted with pending approval details. The app deploys successfully at its current approved config.
1463	
1464	### GitHub Actions error surfacing
1465	
1466	The GitHub Actions workflow emits errors at two levels:
1467	
1468	**Annotations** — for critical errors that require immediate attention. Appear inline in the GitHub Actions UI and on the pull request:
1469	
1470	```
1471	::error title=Deploy failed: my-demo-app::Rollout did not complete within 60s. Check app logs for details.
1472	::error title=Quota exceeded: my-demo-app::repo org/my-repo has reached its app limit (2/2). Contact your platform operator.
1473	```
1474	
1475	**Step output** — full structured error JSON written to the job log for debugging.
1476	
1477	The workflow exits non-zero on any error — GitHub marks the job failed.
1478	
1479	`approval_required` emits a warning annotation — the job succeeds since the app is running at its current approved config:
1480	
1481	```
1482	::warning title=Approval required: my-demo-app::tier change to 'medium' is pending operator approval. App running at current tier 'small'.
1483	```
1484	
1485	### CLI error output
1486	
1487	The CLI formats structured errors for terminal display:
1488	
1489	```
1490	✗ Deploy failed: my-demo-app
1491	  Rollout did not complete within 60s — health checks not passing
1492	  Check app logs: morsel --profile local app logs my-demo-app
1493	```
1494	
1495	```
1496	✗ Quota exceeded: my-demo-app
1497	  repo org/my-repo has reached its app limit (2/2) on the default tier
1498	  Contact your platform operator to request a tier upgrade
1499	```
1500	
1501	Pod logs are never included in error responses. The developer fetches logs separately using the logs endpoint if needed.
1502	
1503	### Deploy failure and rollback
1504	
1505	When a deploy fails (`deploy_failed`), Morsel automatically redeploys the `last-healthy` image digest. The error response includes the operation ID of the rollback so the caller can poll progress:
1506	
1507	```json
1508	{
1509	  "error": {
1510	    "code": "deploy_failed",
1511	    "message": "rollout of my-demo-app did not complete within 60s",
1512	    "remedy": "check app logs for startup errors. rolling back to last healthy image.",
1513	    "context": {
1514	      "failed_image": "sha256:abc123",
1515	      "rollback_image": "sha256:def456",
1516	      "rollback_operation": "op_xyz789"
1517	    }
1518	  }
1519	}
1520	```
1521	
1522	---
1523	
1524	## 16. `morsel lint`
1525	
1526	The `morsel lint` command validates `*.morsel.json` files in the `.morsel/` folder. It is designed to run locally as a pre-commit hook, catching destructive changes before they reach CI.
1527	
1528	### Usage
1529	
1530	```
1531	morsel lint                # validate all .morsel/*.morsel.json files
1532	morsel lint --staged       # validate only git-staged .morsel/*.morsel.json files
1533	morsel lint --fix          # auto-remediate safe issues (schema errors, formatting)
1534	```
1535	
1536	### Pre-commit hook setup
1537	
1538	```bash
1539	# .git/hooks/pre-commit
1540	morsel lint --staged
1541	```
1542	
1543	### What lint checks
1544	
1545	| Check | Severity |
1546	|---|---|
1547	| Schema validity — all required fields present, correct types | Error |
1548	| Valid `type` value (`http`, `worker`, `cronjob`) | Error |
1549	| `schedule` present when `type` is `cronjob` | Error |
1550	| `timeout` present when `type` is `cronjob` | Error |
1551	| `name` unique within `.morsel/` folder | Error |
1552	| Removing a persistence resource marked `permanent: true` | Error |
1553	| Removing a persistence resource marked `permanent: false` | Warning |
1554	| `tier` value within repo's current quota tier | Warning |
1555	| `idle_after` value is a valid duration string | Error |
1556	
1557	### Permanent resource removal
1558	
1559	Attempting to remove a persistence resource marked `permanent: true` is a lint error. The output includes a clear remediation path:
1560	
1561	```
1562	✗ api.morsel.json — removing 'database' which is marked permanent
1563	  Remedy:
1564	    1. Set persistence.database.permanent to false
1565	    2. Deploy
1566	    3. Remove the database declaration in a subsequent commit
1567	```
1568	
1569	This ensures the two-step process (mark transient → deploy → remove) is enforced at the developer's workstation, not in CI. By the time a commit reaches GitHub Actions, lint has already verified the change is safe.
1570	
1571	### Lint in CI
1572	
1573	Lint can also run in CI as an additional gate before the sync and deploy steps:
1574	
1575	```yaml
1576	- name: Lint
1577	  run: morsel lint
1578	```
1579	
1580	A lint failure in CI blocks the deploy without making any changes to the platform.
1581	
1582	---
1583	
1584	## 17. Hibernation
1585	
1586	Apps that receive no traffic for their configured idle threshold are automatically scaled to zero replicas by the Morsel API. Persistence is retained. The app wakes transparently on the next HTTP request via a lightweight Morsel-owned HTTP proxy, which holds the request while the pod starts.
1587	
1588	| Property | Behaviour |
1589	|---|---|
1590	| Idle detection | Morsel API watcher tracks last HTTP activity per app; zero requests for idle threshold triggers scale-to-zero via client-go |
1591	| Wake-on-request | Morsel HTTP proxy holds the first request while the pod initialises |
1592	| Cold start time | Typically 5–15 seconds depending on container image size |
1593	| Persistence during hibernation | All data retained; no cleanup of database or storage |
1594	| Worker hibernation | Workers scale to zero when all queues are empty; Morsel API watcher polls `queue.morsel.internal` depth |
1595	| CronJob hibernation | Morsel API suspends CronJob when app is hibernated; schedule resumes on wake |
1596	
1597	---
1598	
1599	## 18. Platform upgrades
1600	
1601	Platform upgrades are triggered by the operator running `morsel service bootstrap` with a newer binary version. Upgrades are rolling — platform components are upgraded one at a time and apps keep running throughout.
1602	
1603	### Upgrade sequence
1604	
1605	1. **Morsel API** — rolling pod replacement. Brief API unavailability during switchover.
1606	2. **Blob service** — rolling pod replacement. Brief blob service unavailability.
1607	3. **Queue service** — rolling pod replacement. Brief queue service unavailability.
1608	4. **Database service (PGBouncer)** — rolling pod replacement. Brief database proxy unavailability.
1609	5. **Running apps** — redeployed in rolling batches using the stored current image digest with updated platform manifest defaults applied.
1610	6. **Hibernated apps** — manifests updated in place. Apps are not woken.
1611	
1612	GKE Autopilot handles node upgrades transparently and independently — Morsel does not coordinate with GKE node upgrades.
1613	
1614	### App redeployment
1615	
1616	After platform components are upgraded, Morsel redeploys each running app using its stored `current` image digest. This applies updated Kubernetes manifest defaults (resource limits, probe configuration, sidecar versions, network policies) without requiring a new build or developer action.
1617	
1618	What changes on upgrade redeployment:
1619	- Kubernetes manifest defaults from the new platform version
1620	- Sidecar versions (PGBouncer, OTel collector when enabled)
1621	
1622	What does not change:
1623	- The app's container image
1624	- The app's `morsel.json` declarations
1625	- The app's data
1626	
1627	### Failure handling
1628	
1629	If an app redeployment fails during upgrade, Morsel skips it and continues. The upgrade completes for all other apps. Failed apps are listed in the upgrade summary and can be retried individually.
1630	
1631	```
1632	✓ Morsel API upgraded
1633	✓ Blob service upgraded
1634	✓ Queue service upgraded
1635	✓ Database service upgraded
1636	  Redeploying apps...
1637	✓ 47 apps redeployed
1638	✓ 12 hibernated apps updated in place
1639	✗ 3 apps failed — retry with: morsel service upgrade retry
1640	
1641	Failed apps:
1642	  org/team-a / broken-app    rollout timed out
1643	  org/team-b / old-worker    image pull failed
1644	  org/team-c / stale-demo    health check failed
1645	```
1646	
1647	### Retry
1648	
1649	The operator retries failed app redeployments without re-running the full platform upgrade:
1650	
1651	```
1652	morsel [--profile <name>] service upgrade retry
1653	```
1654	
1655	Retries only apps that failed in the most recent upgrade. Retry results are appended to the upgrade report visible in the admin UI.
1656	
1657	### `morsel.json` default changes
1658	
1659	When a new platform version changes `morsel.json` field defaults, the new defaults are applied to all apps on upgrade redeployment. Apps that have explicitly declared a value for the changed field keep their declared value — only apps relying on the platform default are affected.
1660	
1661	---
1662	
1663	## 19. Disaster recovery
1664	
1665	Morsel provides no automated backup or disaster recovery. This is a non-production platform — app owners are responsible for any data they cannot afford to lose. This is stated explicitly in the non-goals.
1666	
1667	### What data exists and where it lives
1668	
1669	| Data | Location | Loss impact |
1670	|---|---|---|
1671	| Morsel platform state | SQLite on a GKE PersistentVolume | Apps still run in Kubernetes but Morsel has no record of them. Recovery requires re-registration via redeploy. |
1672	| App databases | Shared Postgres on a GKE PersistentVolume | App data lost if PV is deleted. Data survives pod rescheduling. |
1673	| Blob storage | GCS bucket (via blob service) | GCS has 99.999999999% durability — data survives platform failures. Lost only if bucket is explicitly deleted. |
1674	| Queue messages | Postgres on a GKE PersistentVolume | Unprocessed messages lost if PV is deleted. |
1675	| App container images | Artifact Registry | Survives platform failures. Lost only if registry is explicitly deleted. |
1676	| Platform secrets | Secret Manager | Survives platform failures. Lost only if secrets are explicitly deleted. |
1677	
1678	### If the Morsel API PersistentVolume is lost
1679	
1680	Morsel's SQLite database is lost. Apps continue running in Kubernetes but Morsel has no record of them. Manual recovery steps:
1681	
1682	1. Morsel API restarts with an empty database
1683	2. Each repo redeploys via `git push` or `morsel app deploy`
1684	3. Redeployment re-registers the repo and app in Morsel's database
1685	4. Quotas and tier assignments are reset to defaults — operator reassigns tiers via admin UI
1686	5. Pending approvals and deploy history are lost
1687	
1688	### If the shared Postgres PersistentVolume is lost
1689	
1690	All app databases and queue messages are lost. The PV loss is detected by PGBouncer and queue service connection failures. Recovery:
1691	
1692	1. Morsel provisions a fresh Postgres instance on a new PV at next startup
1693	2. App databases are recreated empty on next app deploy
1694	3. App owners are responsible for repopulating their data
1695
