1786	      platform.go        # LocalPlatform — no external dependencies
1787	    aws/                 # future
1788	    azure/               # future
1789	```
1790	
1791	### Platform selection
1792	
1793	The active platform is determined at startup from the profile config. `GCPPlatform` is the default; `LocalPlatform` is selected when `morsel service bootstrap --local` is used.
1794	
1795	```json
1796	{
1797	  "platform": "gcp",
1798	  "project": "morsel-prod",
1799	  ...
1800	}
1801	```
1802	
1803	No business logic code path branches on platform — all branching is encapsulated within the platform implementations themselves.
1804	
1805	---
1806	
1807	## 21. Local mode
1808	
1809	Local mode runs a full Morsel replica on a developer's machine for testing and development. It is implemented as `LocalPlatform` — a complete implementation of the `Platform` interface with no cloud dependencies. All platform behaviour including hibernation, quotas, and approvals is enforced identically to production.
1810	
1811	### Prerequisites
1812	
1813	Local mode requires a local Kubernetes cluster. Morsel does not install or manage one. On bootstrap, `LocalPlatform` checks for a kubeconfig at `~/.kube/config` or `$KUBECONFIG` and uses the current context.
1814	
1815	If no cluster is found, Morsel prints instructions and exits cleanly:
1816	
1817	```
1818	morsel --profile local service bootstrap --platform local
1819	
1820	Checking for local Kubernetes...
1821	  ✗ No local Kubernetes found.
1822	
1823	  Install one of the following and re-run:
1824	    • Docker Desktop  https://docs.docker.com/desktop/
1825	    • Rancher Desktop https://rancherdesktop.io
1826	    • k3s             https://k3s.io
1827	    • minikube        https://minikube.sigs.k8s.io
1828	
1829	  Morsel looks for a kubeconfig at ~/.kube/config or $KUBECONFIG.
1830	```
1831	
1832	If a cluster is found, bootstrap proceeds:
1833	
1834	```
1835	morsel --profile local service bootstrap --platform local
1836	
1837	Checking for local Kubernetes...
1838	  ✓ Found Docker Desktop Kubernetes (v1.29) — using this cluster
1839	```
1840	
1841	### LocalPlatform implementation
1842	
1843	| Concern | Implementation |
1844	|---|---|
1845	| `BlobStore` | Filesystem under `~/.morsel/local/blobs/{namespace}/{key}` |
1846	| `SecretStore` | Local JSON file at `~/.morsel/local/secrets.json` |
1847	| `CredentialProvider` | No-op — no cloud authentication required |
1848	| `DNSProvider` | `*.morsel.localhost` — resolves to `127.0.0.1` in all modern browsers. No configuration needed. |
1849	| `CertProvider` | Self-signed certificate generated at bootstrap time |
1850	| Kubernetes | `client-go` against current kubeconfig context |
1851	| Container registry | Local registry container deployed into the cluster |
1852	
1853	### App URLs
1854	
1855	Apps running in local mode use the `*.morsel.localhost` domain:
1856	
1857	```
1858	Named app:    https://{app-name}.{repo-slug}.morsel.localhost
1859	Unnamed app:  https://{repo-slug}.morsel.localhost
1860	```
1861	
1862	No DNS configuration required — `*.morsel.localhost` resolves natively.
1863	
1864	### Authentication
1865	
1866	Local mode has no IAP. `morsel service login --platform local` issues a local operator-role Morsel token directly — the developer is always the operator of their local instance. No browser OAuth flow is triggered.
1867	
1868	### Deploying apps locally
1869	
1870	Since GitHub Actions does not run locally, developers use the Morsel CLI to deploy directly:
1871	
1872	```
1873	morsel --profile local app deploy
1874	```
1875	
1876	`morsel app deploy` is the local equivalent of the GitHub Actions workflow. It runs the following steps:
1877	
1878	1. Discovers all `*.morsel.json` files in `.morsel/`
1879	2. Calls `POST /api/repos/:slug/sync` with the full app list — Morsel detects any deletions
1880	3. Builds each app's container image in parallel using the local Docker or Podman daemon, from the current working directory
1881	4. Pushes each image directly to the in-cluster local registry
1882	5. Uses the stored local profile token — no GitHub OIDC exchange needed
1883	6. Calls `POST /api/repos/:slug/apps` for each app with the image digest
1884	
1885	**Builds from the working directory**, including uncommitted changes. This is intentional — local development benefits from testing the current state of code, not just what is committed.
1886	
1887	**No staging handshake.** In production, GitHub Actions pushes to a staging registry and the Morsel API copies to the canonical registry to prevent direct writes. Locally the developer and the Morsel API share the same trust boundary, so `morsel app deploy` pushes directly to the in-cluster registry. Simpler and faster.
1888	
1889	**Requirements:**
1890	- Docker or Podman running locally
1891	- A `Dockerfile` at the repo root or at a path declared in the app declaration
1892	- A valid local profile token (`morsel service login` if needed)
1893	
1894	`morsel app deploy` works against both local and cloud platform profiles. When running in a GitHub Actions environment (`GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`), the command uses the platform's `DeployCredentials()` to obtain the appropriate token and registry auth for that platform. The deploy logic is identical regardless of platform — the `Platform` interface abstracts all credential and registry differences.
1895	
1896	### Full replica behaviour
1897	
1898	Local mode enforces all production platform behaviour:
1899	
1900	| Feature | Local behaviour |
1901	|---|---|
1902	| Hibernation | Fully enforced — apps scale to zero after idle threshold |
1903	| Quotas | Fully enforced — deploy API rejects apps over tier limits |
1904	| Approvals | Fully enforced — developer is also operator, so they approve their own requests |
1905	| Permanent resources | Fully enforced |
1906	| Lint | Identical to production |
1907	| Sync | Identical to production |
1908	
1909	The developer approving their own approval requests is intentional — it exercises the full approval workflow locally without requiring a separate operator account.
1910	
1911	### Local bootstrap prompts
1912	
1913	`LocalPlatform.BootstrapPrompts()` returns a minimal set:
1914	
1915	| Prompt | Default | Notes |
1916	|---|---|---|
1917	| GitHub org slug | None — required | Used to scope OIDC token validation |
1918	| Local domain | `morsel.localhost` | Base domain for app URLs |
1919	
1920	No cloud credentials, no region, no DNS provider, no budget configuration.
1921	
1922	---
1923	
1924	## 22. Portability note
1925	
1926	Morsel is designed for GCP and is not being built for multi-cloud. However, the platform abstraction (section 17) makes a future AWS or Azure implementation a well-scoped addition rather than a redesign.
1927	
1928	Adding a new cloud means implementing the `Platform` interface — `AWSPlatform` or `AzurePlatform` — in an isolated package. No business logic changes. The bootstrap binary gains a new platform selection path. The admin UI auth mechanism (currently GCP IAP) is the most cloud-specific concern not covered by the `Platform` interface; Cloudflare Access is a cloud-agnostic alternative worth considering if portability becomes a requirement.
1929	
1930	No multi-cloud work should be undertaken without revisiting this note and making a deliberate decision to proceed.
1931	
1932	---
1933	
1934	## 23. Key decisions log
1935	
1936	| Requirement | Decision | Rationale |
1937	|---|---|---|
1938	| Infrastructure | GKE (full Kubernetes control plane) | Scale target (50+ users, 500+ apps) rules out simpler managed options. Designer is comfortable with K8s complexity. |
1939	| Manifest apply | Morsel API via client-go | Direct apply on each deploy is sufficient for Morsel's controlled deploy model. |
1940	| Hibernation | Native Morsel API watcher + HTTP proxy | Watcher goroutine tracks activity and issues scale commands; lightweight proxy handles wake-on-request. |
1941	| Certificate management | Native via Go ACME library + Let's Encrypt | Morsel API handles provisioning and renewal directly. |
1942	| DNS management | Native via Cloud DNS and Cloudflare Go SDKs | Morsel API creates and removes records on deploy and delete. |
1943	| GitHub integration | Push model (GitHub calls Morsel) | OIDC tokens are short-lived, carry no org-level access, and require no credentials stored on either side. |
1944	| App ownership | GitHub repo | The repo is verifiable directly from the OIDC token `repository` claim. No GitHub API calls required. Access follows repo access automatically. |
1945	| Repo onboarding | Automatic with default quota | Manual onboarding is high operator burden. Automatic onboarding with a low default quota bounds cost exposure without blocking developers. |
1946	| Quota tiers | Three tiers: default, standard, power; tracked per repo | Coarse tiers are easier to explain and administer than per-app limits. Default auto-assigned; upper tiers require operator action. |
1947	| Operator tooling | `morsel` CLI + admin UI (static site on GCS); no external dependencies | Operator may rotate and has no cloud knowledge. kubectl, gcloud, and Terraform are not acceptable operator interfaces. Admin UI served as a static bundle from GCS — no dedicated pod required. |
1948	| Bootstrap implementation | GCP Go SDK + client-go embedded in `morsel` binary | Binary is fully self-contained. Behaviour is deterministic and debuggable. |
1949	| Bootstrap configuration | Secret Manager secret (`morsel-bootstrap-config`) | No dedicated storage resource required. Platform configuration is not tied to a specific operator's machine. Secret Manager is already provisioned for Morsel's own secrets. |
1950	| CLI profile model | `~/.config/morsel/<profile>.profile.json`, selected via `--profile` flag | Supports multiple Morsel instances per operator without magic context switching. File created only on successful authentication. `0600` permissions. |
1951	| Bootstrap auth | GCP OAuth flow with localhost callback | No gcloud required. Operator needs only a browser. Token held in memory only; not persisted. |
1952	| App persistence | GCS (via blob service), in-cluster Postgres (database + queue service) | All persistence backed by in-cluster or GCS storage. No managed GCP messaging service required. |
1953	| Morsel API storage | SQLite on a GKE Persistent Volume | Morsel's own data is light — repos, apps, image digests. No managed database service required. Single replica with single writer by design. Brief unavailability on pod rescheduling is acceptable for a non-production platform. |
1954	| DNS / TLS | Morsel API + Let's Encrypt; Cloud DNS or Cloudflare | Fully automated; zero operator involvement in cert renewal or DNS record management. Cloudflare supported for organisations already using it as their primary DNS provider. |
1955	| Container registry | Single private Artifact Registry repository; push isolation enforced by Morsel API | Simpler IAM than per-repo repositories. Repos never write to the canonical registry directly. Morsel API is the sole writer. |
1956	| Registry push model | Staging handshake: GitHub Actions → staging repo → Morsel copies to canonical | GitHub Actions never touches the canonical registry. Cross-repo overwrites are impossible regardless of registry ACLs. |
1957	| Rollback | Morsel retains current + last-healthy digest per app | Minimal storage footprint. Rollback is a Morsel-internal operation requiring no registry credential by GitHub Actions. |
1958	| GCP credentials | Workload Identity throughout; no service account key files | Nothing to rotate, nothing to leak. Zero stored secrets for platform-level access. |
1959	| GCP isolation | Dedicated GCP project; no cross-project IAM grants | Blast radius of a full Morsel compromise is bounded to the Morsel project. Operator's wider infrastructure is unreachable. |
1960	| Network | Private Google Access for all GCP service traffic | GCP API endpoints unreachable from internet. Only outbound leg (GitHub Actions → GCP) traverses internet, secured by OIDC. |
1961	| Self-hosted runners | Explicitly out of scope | Operational cost of runner lifecycle management not justified for a non-production platform. |
1962	| Hibernation idle threshold | Per-app `idle_after` field in app declaration; platform-wide default set in wizard | Per-app gives developers control over their own cold-start tradeoff. Platform default keeps the operator in control of the baseline. |
1963	| Morsel's own secrets | GCP Secret Manager (3–4 secrets: signing key, notification config, bootstrap config, Cloudflare token if applicable) | Morsel API accesses a fixed, small set of secrets at startup via Workload Identity + Go SDK. No database credentials required — SQLite has no auth layer. |
1964	| Token model | Short-lived access token (JWT) + long-lived refresh token | Access token verified by signature — no DB lookup per request. Role encoded in token; changes take effect within one TTL. Refresh token rotated on every use. |
1965	| Access token TTL | 15 minutes (operator configurable) | Short enough that role changes propagate quickly. Long enough to be practical without constant refresh. |
1966	| GitHub Actions token | 10-minute access token, no refresh token | Workflow re-exchanges on every run. No stored credential needed. |
1967	| Refresh token lifetime | 90 days | Practical for CLI use. Revocation is a single SQLite delete. |
1968	| RBAC | Role encoded in token; two roles: operator and developer | Operator role determined at exchange time by matching Google identity against bootstrap-configured operator principal. Repo encoded from OIDC `repository` claim. No per-request directory lookup. |
1969	| App naming | Unique within repo; unnamed app gets repo slug as name | Allows single-app repos to have a clean URL (`repo.apps.example.com`) while multi-app repos use `name.repo.apps.example.com`. |
1970	| App declaration | `.morsel/` folder with `*.morsel.json` files | One file per app. Composable — add or remove apps by adding or removing files. Workflow discovers all files at deploy time. |
1971	| Multi-app deploy | GitHub Actions matrix job, parallel, fail-fast disabled | Apps in a repo are independent. One failing deploy does not block others. |
1972	| Upsert | Single `POST /api/repos/:slug/apps` for create and update | Caller always sends full desired state. Morsel determines from its own records whether this is a create or update. Consistent workflow regardless of app age. |
1973	| Destructive persistence changes | Blocked by default; `?force=true` (operator only) to override | Prevents accidental data loss. Lint catches violations locally before CI. |
1974	| Orphaned apps | Defined as apps whose GitHub repo has been deleted or archived. No automated detection — open problem. | Morsel holds no GitHub token and receives no webhook events. Operator performs periodic manual review via stale apps list in admin UI. |
1975	| Platform abstraction | Single `Platform` interface with `GCPPlatform` and `LocalPlatform` implementations | All cloud SDK calls isolated in platform packages. Business logic has no cloud dependencies. Adding AWS or Azure support means implementing the interface — nothing else changes. |
1976	| Bootstrap wizard | Platform-agnostic prompt/answer loop | Wizard presents prompts returned by `Platform.BootstrapPrompts()` and passes answers to `Platform.Bootstrap()`. Platform owns its own onboarding questions, OAuth flows, and resource planning. Wizard never branches on platform. |
1977	| GitHub Actions workflow | Single copy-paste workflow file, triggered on push to default branch | Thin wrapper — authentication and dispatch only. `morsel app deploy` owns all deploy logic. Platform abstraction keeps workflow identical regardless of cloud platform. |
1978	| `morsel app deploy` in CI | Detected via `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`, uses `Platform.DeployCredentials()` | Same command for local and CI. Platform handles credential and registry differences. No separate CI-specific command needed. |
1979	| Backups | None — no automated backup or disaster recovery | Non-production platform. App owners responsible for data they cannot afford to lose. Recovery path documented for PV loss scenarios. |
1980	| Platform upgrade strategy | Rolling — platform components upgraded one at a time, apps redeployed with new defaults | Apps keep running throughout. Hibernated apps updated in place without waking. No maintenance window required. |
1981	| Upgrade failure handling | Skip and continue — failed apps listed in upgrade report, operator retries individually | A single app failure does not block platform upgrade. `morsel service upgrade retry` retries only failed apps. |
1982	| Local Kubernetes | Detect existing cluster via kubeconfig; print instructions and exit if none found | Morsel does not install or manage a local Kubernetes. Complexity of cross-platform k3s management not justified for a developer tool. |
1983	| Local mode scope | Full production replica | Hibernation, quotas, and approvals all enforced locally. Prevents surprises in CI that cannot be reproduced locally. |
1984	| `morsel app deploy` | Local platform profiles only | Replaces GitHub Actions for local development. Not available against cloud instances — use GitHub Actions for those. |
1985	| Blob storage API | `blob.morsel.internal` — GET, PUT, list with prefix and cursor | Apps never touch GCS directly. GCS naming complexity hidden. Quota enforced at API layer. Namespace isolation via pod identity. |
1986	| Blob/database quotas | Separate independent limits per tier | Different cost profiles. Hitting one does not affect the other. Both individually overridable via approval workflow. |
1987	| Database | Shared in-cluster Postgres, one database per app, PGBouncer sidecar | Developer sees fixed constants. Real per-app credentials held by PGBouncer sidecar, never visible to app. |
1988	| Database isolation | Per-app Postgres user with GRANT scoped to own database only | App cannot access another app's database regardless of what it attempts. Kubernetes NetworkPolicy prevents pod-to-pod sidecar access. |
1989	| Queue service | `queue.morsel.internal` backed by Postgres tables | No GCP Pub/Sub required. App creates queues at runtime — no declaration of queue names needed. Quota on total storage across all app queues. |
1990	| Queue semantics | Queue only (no topics/fan-out) | Point-to-point delivery sufficient for non-production use cases. Simpler to implement and reason about. |
1991	| App-to-app communication | Public HTTPS URLs only | No private inter-app channel. Private apps (`private: true`) act as VPC-internal services accessible to other Morsel apps. |
1992	| Health checks | Standard Kubernetes liveness and readiness probes; defaults `/livez` and `/healthz` | Morsel configures probes and defers all behaviour to Kubernetes. Deploy success tied to rollout status. No custom Morsel probe logic. |
1993	| Error responses | Structured JSON with `code`, `message`, `remedy`, `context` | Formatting is the client's responsibility. API provides stable machine-readable codes. `remedy` always present — no error without a path forward. |
1994	| GitHub Actions error surfacing | Annotations for critical errors, step output for details | Annotations surface inline in GitHub UI. Full structured JSON in job log for debugging. `approval_required` emits warning annotation — job still succeeds. |
1995	| Pod logs in errors | Not included | Developer fetches logs separately. Prevents accidental sensitive data leakage through deploy pipeline. |
1996	| CronJob retries | Default 0 — fail fast | Developer opts in to retries explicitly via `retries` field. Failure surfaced immediately with exit code and stderr. |
1997	| Worker hibernation | All queues must report `idle: true` | Morsel watches all queues; worker stays alive if any queue has external messages pending. |
1998	| Self-consuming queue detection | Rolling window of last N messages; `idle: true` when 100% self-consumed | Prevents a worker from keeping itself alive by consuming its own messages. N is platform-configurable (default 100). Exposed as single `idle` boolean on queue. |
1999	| Permanent resources | Per-resource `permanent` flag in app declaration, default false | Prevents accidental deletion of stateful resources on app or repo deletion. Removal requires two-step process enforced by lint. |
2000	| Database engine | Postgres only | Single engine simplifies operations. |
2001	| Destructive change guard | lint (local/CI) + operator-only `?force=true` | Lint catches destructive changes before they reach CI. Force flag is an operator escape hatch only — developers receive 403. |
2002	| Sync endpoint | `POST /api/repos/:slug/sync` called once per workflow before deploys | Gives Morsel a complete view of declared apps at each git SHA. Enables deletion of removed apps without requiring explicit delete calls from the workflow. |
2003	| morsel lint | CLI command with `--staged` and `--fix` flags | Designed as a pre-commit hook. Catches schema errors and permanent resource violations locally before CI. |
2004	| Protected config | Subset of fields require operator approval before applying | Developers declare desired state freely; protected fields are queued for approval. App runs in best achievable state with currently approved config. |
2005	| Approval granularity | Per resource field | Operator can approve a tier change independently of a quota increase. Changes reconcile as approved. |
2006	| Approval expiry | Configurable, default 30 days | Stale approvals are automatically rejected and cleared. Developer resubmits if still needed. |
2007	| Batch approvals | Single `POST /api/operator/approvals/batch` | Operator actions a set of approvals in one call. Approved changes per app applied in a single reconciliation pass. `ignore` defers without rejecting. |
2008	| Admin UI authentication | GCP Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) | No password to manage or rotate. Operator authenticates with their existing Google account. |
2009	| Operator principals | Google account or Google Group; either accepted | Groups suit organisations with a stable operator team; individuals suit smaller setups. IAP treats both identically. Managed via `morsel service operator` subcommands; no Morsel involvement in group membership. |
2010	
2011	---
2012	
2013	## 24. GitHub Actions workflow
2014	
2015	Developers copy a single workflow file verbatim into their repository. No customisation is required beyond setting four repository-level variables once.
2016	
2017	### Repository variables
2018	
2019	Set these once per repository in GitHub → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Variables:
2020	
2021	| Variable | Description | Provided by |
2022	|---|---|---|
2023	| `MORSEL_API_URL` | Morsel instance URL, e.g. `https://admin.apps.example.com` | Operator |
2024	| `MORSEL_GCP_PROJECT` | GCP project ID of the Morsel instance | Operator |
2025	| `MORSEL_WIF_PROVIDER` | Workload Identity Federation provider resource name | Operator |
2026	| `MORSEL_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` | GCP service account email for GitHub Actions | Operator |
2027	
2028	### Workflow file
2029	
2030	Save as `.github/workflows/morsel-deploy.yml`:
2031	
2032	```yaml
2033	name: Deploy to Morsel
2034	
2035	on:
2036	  push:
2037	    branches: [main]
2038	
2039	permissions:
2040	  id-token: write   # required for GitHub OIDC token
2041	  contents: read
2042	
2043	jobs:
2044	  deploy:
2045	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
2046	
2047	    steps:
2048	      - name: Checkout
2049	        uses: actions/checkout@v4
2050	
2051	      - name: Install morsel CLI
2052	        run: |
2053	          curl -L https://github.com/org/morsel/releases/latest/download/morsel-Linux-x86_64 \
2054	            -o morsel && chmod +x morsel && sudo mv morsel /usr/local/bin/morsel
2055	
2056	      - name: Deploy
2057	        env:
2058	          MORSEL_API_URL: ${{ vars.MORSEL_API_URL }}
2059	          MORSEL_GCP_PROJECT: ${{ vars.MORSEL_GCP_PROJECT }}
2060	          MORSEL_WIF_PROVIDER: ${{ vars.MORSEL_WIF_PROVIDER }}
2061	          MORSEL_SERVICE_ACCOUNT: ${{ vars.MORSEL_SERVICE_ACCOUNT }}
2062	        run: morsel app deploy
2063	```
2064	
2065	### What `morsel app deploy` does in CI
2066	
2067	When `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`, the CLI detects it is running in CI and adapts:
2068	
2069	1. Calls `Platform.DeployCredentials()` — on `GCPPlatform` this exchanges the GitHub OIDC token for a Morsel access token via WIF and obtains registry push credentials
2070	2. Discovers all `*.morsel.json` files in `.morsel/`
2071	3. Calls `POST /api/repos/:slug/sync` with the full app list
2072	4. For each app in parallel:
2073	   - Builds the container image using Docker (available on `ubuntu-latest`)
2074	   - Pushes to the staging Artifact Registry repository
2075	   - Calls `POST /api/repos/:slug/apps` with the image digest and Morsel token
2076	5. Emits GitHub Actions annotations for errors and approval warnings
2077	6. Exits non-zero on any deploy failure
2078	
2079	### Job output
2080	
2081	Successful deploy:
2082	```
2083	✓ Synced 3 apps (0 deleted)
2084	✓ my-demo-app       deployed sha256:abc123
2085	✓ worker            deployed sha256:def456
2086	⚠ scheduler         tier change to 'medium' pending operator approval — running at 'small'
2087	```
2088	
2089	Failed deploy:
2090	```
2091	✓ Synced 3 apps (0 deleted)
2092	✓ my-demo-app       deployed sha256:abc123
2093	✗ worker            deploy failed — rollout timed out. Rolling back to sha256:prev456
2094	✓ scheduler         deployed sha256:ghi789
2095	```
2096	
2097	### Dockerfile requirement
2098	
2099	Each app must have a `Dockerfile` at the repository root, or declare a custom path in the app declaration (future field — not yet implemented). The workflow builds from the repository root context.
2100	
2101	---
2102	
2103	## 25. Open questions
2104	
2105	- **Observability** — deferred. Stack selected (OTel collector, Loki, Prometheus, Tempo, Grafana) but integration details not yet designed: Grafana auth and user management, retention policies, local mode equivalent, backup of observability data, quota model for ingest rates. The `observability` field is reserved in `morsel.json` for future use.
2106	
2107	---
2108	
2109	## 26. Iterative build plan
2110	
2111	The platform is built incrementally. Each phase is independently useful and testable before the next begins.
2112	
2113	| Phase | Scope |
2114	|---|---|
2115	| 1 — Foundation | `morsel service bootstrap`: GCP OAuth, preflight checks, wizard, GCP resource provisioning (VPC, GKE Autopilot, Artifact Registry, Secret Manager, IAM, WIF, IAP), GKE Persistent Volume for SQLite; platform secrets and bootstrap config written to Secret Manager |
2116	| 1b — Platform abstraction | `Platform` interface: `BootstrapPrompts()`, `BootstrapPlan()`, `Bootstrap()`, `BlobStore`, `SecretStore`, `CredentialProvider`, `DNSProvider`, `CertProvider`; `GCPPlatform` and `LocalPlatform` implementations |
2117	| 1c — Local mode | `LocalPlatform`: filesystem blob store, local secrets, no-op credentials, `*.morsel.localhost` DNS, self-signed certs, local registry, `morsel app deploy` CLI command |
2118	| 2 — Morsel API: auth | Token exchange endpoints (`/api/token/github-oidc`, `/api/token/gcp-oidc`, `/api/token/refresh`), JWT signing, refresh token store in SQLite, RBAC middleware |
2119	| 2b — Error handling | Structured error response model, error codes, rollback on deploy_failed, GitHub Actions annotation format |
2120	| 3 — Morsel API: deploy | GitHub OIDC validation, sync endpoint, staging handshake, image copy + rollback slot management, repo auto-registration, quota enforcement, direct manifest apply via client-go, permanent resource handling, protected config approval workflow |
2121	| 4 — Morsel API: networking | GKE Gateway API wiring, internal/external ingress, ACME certificate provisioning and renewal via Go ACME library, DNS record management via Cloud DNS and Cloudflare SDKs |
2122	| 5 — Morsel API: persistence | GCS bucket provisioning (for blob service) |
2123	| 6 — Morsel API: hibernation | Activity watcher goroutine, scale-to-zero via client-go, HTTP proxy for wake-on-request |
2124	| 6b — morsel lint | CLI lint command: schema validation, permanent resource checks, --staged and --fix flags |
2125	| 7 — Admin UI | Static React SPA deployed to GCS; app list, repo management, quota promotion, cost dashboard |
2126	| 8 — Hardening | Audit logging, `morsel service bootstrap` upgrade behaviour, `morsel service upgrade retry`, `morsel service status`, `morsel service delete`, `morsel service operator` subcommands, disaster recovery note, operator handover docs |
2127	
2128	Each phase will produce a working, reviewable increment. Design decisions specific to a phase will be captured as addenda to this document before that phase begins.

### Reducing risk without formal backups

While Morsel provides no automated backups, operators can reduce risk with minimal effort:

- Enable GKE Autopilot's PersistentVolume automatic snapshots via GCP Backup for GKE — a GCP-managed feature the operator can enable independently of Morsel
- GCS blob data is inherently durable and requires no additional protection
- Secret Manager data is inherently durable

---

## 20. Platform abstraction

All infrastructure concerns in Morsel are accessed through a single `Platform` interface. Business logic never imports a cloud SDK directly — platform-specific implementations live in isolated packages and are injected at startup.

### Interface

```go
type Platform interface {
    // Bootstrap lifecycle
    BootstrapPrompts() []Prompt
    BootstrapPlan(answers map[string]string) Plan
    Bootstrap(answers map[string]string) error

    // Deploy lifecycle
    DeployCredentials(ctx context.Context) (DeployCredentials, error)
    StagingRegistry() string

    // Runtime infrastructure
    Blobs()       BlobStore
    Secrets()     SecretStore
    Credentials() CredentialProvider
    DNS()         DNSProvider
    Certs()       CertProvider
}

type DeployCredentials struct {
    MorselToken  string   // exchanged from platform-specific token
    RegistryAuth string   // registry push credentials
}
```

type Prompt struct {
    Key         string
    Label       string
    Description string
    Default     string
    Required    bool
    Secret      bool                // mask input in terminal
    Validate    func(string) error  // optional inline validation
}

type Plan struct {
    Summary   string     // human-readable description of what will be created
    Resources []Resource // list of resources with estimated costs
}
```

Each method covers one concern:

| Method / Interface | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `BootstrapPrompts()` | Returns prompts for the wizard to present. Platform owns its own onboarding questions. |
| `BootstrapPlan()` | Returns a human-readable plan of what will be created, given the operator's answers. |
| `Bootstrap()` | Performs platform authentication and full provisioning. |
| `BlobStore` | Object storage — get, put, list, delete, usage |
| `SecretStore` | Platform secret read and write |
| `CredentialProvider` | Service authentication (Workload Identity or equivalent) |
| `DNSProvider` | DNS record create and delete |
| `CertProvider` | TLS certificate provisioning and renewal |

### Implementations

| Implementation | Use | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GCPPlatform` | Production | GCS, Secret Manager, Workload Identity, Cloud DNS or Cloudflare, ACME/Let's Encrypt. `DeployCredentials()` exchanges GitHub OIDC for Morsel token via WIF. |
| `LocalPlatform` | Local development | Filesystem blobs, local JSON secrets, no-op credentials, `*.morsel.localhost`, self-signed certs. `DeployCredentials()` reads stored local profile token. |
| `AWSPlatform` | Future | S3, Secrets Manager, IRSA, Route 53, ACME/Let's Encrypt |
| `AzurePlatform` | Future | Azure Blob, Key Vault, Azure Workload Identity, Azure DNS, ACME/Let's Encrypt |

### Package structure

The `Platform` interface is defined in a package with no cloud SDK dependencies. Each implementation lives in its own package and imports only what it needs. The Morsel API, blob service, queue service, and bootstrap binary all receive a `Platform` at startup via dependency injection.

```
morsel/
  platform/
    platform.go          # interface definitions only — no cloud SDK imports
    gcp/
      platform.go        # GCPPlatform — imports GCP SDKs
    local/
      platform.go        # LocalPlatform — no external dependencies
    aws/                 # future
    azure/               # future
```

### Platform selection

The active platform is determined at startup from the profile config. `GCPPlatform` is the default; `LocalPlatform` is selected when `morsel service bootstrap --local` is used.

```json
{
  "platform": "gcp",
  "project": "morsel-prod",
  ...
}
```

No business logic code path branches on platform — all branching is encapsulated within the platform implementations themselves.

## 21. Local mode

Local mode runs a full Morsel replica on a developer's machine for testing and development. It is implemented as `LocalPlatform` — a complete implementation of the `Platform` interface with no cloud dependencies. All platform behaviour including hibernation, quotas, and approvals is enforced identically to production.

### Prerequisites

Local mode requires a local Kubernetes cluster. Morsel does not install or manage one. On bootstrap, `LocalPlatform` checks for a kubeconfig at `~/.kube/config` or `$KUBECONFIG` and uses the current context.

If no cluster is found, Morsel prints instructions and exits cleanly:

```
morsel --profile local service bootstrap --platform local

Checking for local Kubernetes...
  ✗ No local Kubernetes found.

  Install one of the following and re-run:
    • Docker Desktop  https://docs.docker.com/desktop/
    • Rancher Desktop https://rancherdesktop.io
    • k3s             https://k3s.io
    • minikube        https://minikube.sigs.k8s.io

  Morsel looks for a kubeconfig at ~/.kube/config or $KUBECONFIG.
```

If a cluster is found, bootstrap proceeds:

```
morsel --profile local service bootstrap --platform local

Checking for local Kubernetes...
  ✓ Found Docker Desktop Kubernetes (v1.29) — using this cluster
```

### LocalPlatform implementation

| Concern | Implementation |
|---|---|
| `BlobStore` | Filesystem under `~/.morsel/local/blobs/{namespace}/{key}` |
| `SecretStore` | Local JSON file at `~/.morsel/local/secrets.json` |
| `CredentialProvider` | No-op — no cloud authentication required |
| `DNSProvider` | `*.morsel.localhost` — resolves to `127.0.0.1` in all modern browsers. No configuration needed. |
| `CertProvider` | Self-signed certificate generated at bootstrap time |
| Kubernetes | `client-go` against current kubeconfig context |
| Container registry | Local registry container deployed into the cluster |

### App URLs

Apps running in local mode use the `*.morsel.localhost` domain:

```
Named app:    https://{app-name}.{repo-slug}.morsel.localhost
Unnamed app:  https://{repo-slug}.morsel.localhost
```

No DNS configuration required — `*.morsel.localhost` resolves natively.

### Authentication

Local mode has no IAP. `morsel service login --platform local` issues a local operator-role Morsel token directly — the developer is always the operator of their local instance. No browser OAuth flow is triggered.

### Deploying apps locally

Since GitHub Actions does not run locally, developers use the Morsel CLI to deploy directly:

```
morsel --profile local app deploy
```

`morsel app deploy` is the local equivalent of the GitHub Actions workflow. It runs the following steps:

1. Discovers all `*.morsel.json` files in `.morsel/`
2. Calls `POST /api/repos/:slug/sync` with the full app list — Morsel detects any deletions
3. Builds each app's container image in parallel using the local Docker or Podman daemon, from the current working directory
4. Pushes each image directly to the in-cluster local registry
5. Uses the stored local profile token — no GitHub OIDC exchange needed
6. Calls `POST /api/repos/:slug/apps` for each app with the image digest

**Builds from the working directory**, including uncommitted changes. This is intentional — local development benefits from testing the current state of code, not just what is committed.

**No staging handshake.** In production, GitHub Actions pushes to a staging registry and the Morsel API copies to the canonical registry to prevent direct writes. Locally the developer and the Morsel API share the same trust boundary, so `morsel app deploy` pushes directly to the in-cluster registry. Simpler and faster.

**Requirements:**
- Docker or Podman running locally
- A `Dockerfile` at the repo root or at a path declared in the app declaration
- A valid local profile token (`morsel service login` if needed)

`morsel app deploy` works against both local and cloud platform profiles. When running in a GitHub Actions environment (`GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`), the command uses the platform's `DeployCredentials()` to obtain the appropriate token and registry auth for that platform. The deploy logic is identical regardless of platform — the `Platform` interface abstracts all credential and registry differences.

### Full replica behaviour

Local mode enforces all production platform behaviour:

| Feature | Local behaviour |
|---|---|
| Hibernation | Fully enforced — apps scale to zero after idle threshold |
| Quotas | Fully enforced — deploy API rejects apps over tier limits |
| Approvals | Fully enforced — developer is also operator, so they approve their own requests |
| Permanent resources | Fully enforced |
| Lint | Identical to production |
| Sync | Identical to production |

The developer approving their own approval requests is intentional — it exercises the full approval workflow locally without requiring a separate operator account.

### Local bootstrap prompts

`LocalPlatform.BootstrapPrompts()` returns a minimal set:

| Prompt | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| GitHub org slug | None — required | Used to scope OIDC token validation |
| Local domain | `morsel.localhost` | Base domain for app URLs |

No cloud credentials, no region, no DNS provider, no budget configuration.

---

## 22. Portability note

Morsel is designed for GCP and is not being built for multi-cloud. However, the platform abstraction (section 17) makes a future AWS or Azure implementation a well-scoped addition rather than a redesign.

Adding a new cloud means implementing the `Platform` interface — `AWSPlatform` or `AzurePlatform` — in an isolated package. No business logic changes. The bootstrap binary gains a new platform selection path. The admin UI auth mechanism (currently GCP IAP) is the most cloud-specific concern not covered by the `Platform` interface; Cloudflare Access is a cloud-agnostic alternative worth considering if portability becomes a requirement.

No multi-cloud work should be undertaken without revisiting this note and making a deliberate decision to proceed.

---

## 23. Key decisions log

| Requirement | Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Infrastructure | GKE (full Kubernetes control plane) | Scale target (50+ users, 500+ apps) rules out simpler managed options. Designer is comfortable with K8s complexity. |
| Manifest apply | Morsel API via client-go | Direct apply on each deploy is sufficient for Morsel's controlled deploy model. |
| Hibernation | Native Morsel API watcher + HTTP proxy | Watcher goroutine tracks activity and issues scale commands; lightweight proxy handles wake-on-request. |
| Certificate management | Native via Go ACME library + Let's Encrypt | Morsel API handles provisioning and renewal directly. |
| DNS management | Native via Cloud DNS and Cloudflare Go SDKs | Morsel API creates and removes records on deploy and delete. |
| GitHub integration | Push model (GitHub calls Morsel) | OIDC tokens are short-lived, carry no org-level access, and require no credentials stored on either side. |
| App ownership | GitHub repo | The repo is verifiable directly from the OIDC token `repository` claim. No GitHub API calls required. Access follows repo access automatically. |
| Repo onboarding | Automatic with default quota | Manual onboarding is high operator burden. Automatic onboarding with a low default quota bounds cost exposure without blocking developers. |
| Quota tiers | Three tiers: default, standard, power; tracked per repo | Coarse tiers are easier to explain and administer than per-app limits. Default auto-assigned; upper tiers require operator action. |
| Operator tooling | `morsel` CLI + admin UI (static site on GCS); no external dependencies | Operator may rotate and has no cloud knowledge. kubectl, gcloud, and Terraform are not acceptable operator interfaces. Admin UI served as a static bundle from GCS — no dedicated pod required. |
| Bootstrap implementation | GCP Go SDK + client-go embedded in `morsel` binary | Binary is fully self-contained. Behaviour is deterministic and debuggable. |
| Bootstrap configuration | Secret Manager secret (`morsel-bootstrap-config`) | No dedicated storage resource required. Platform configuration is not tied to a specific operator's machine. Secret Manager is already provisioned for Morsel's own secrets. |
| CLI profile model | `~/.config/morsel/<profile>.profile.json`, selected via `--profile` flag | Supports multiple Morsel instances per operator without magic context switching. File created only on successful authentication. `0600` permissions. |
| Bootstrap auth | GCP OAuth flow with localhost callback | No gcloud required. Operator needs only a browser. Token held in memory only; not persisted. |
| App persistence | GCS (via blob service), in-cluster Postgres (database + queue service) | All persistence backed by in-cluster or GCS storage. No managed GCP messaging service required. |
| Morsel API storage | SQLite on a GKE Persistent Volume | Morsel's own data is light — repos, apps, image digests. No managed database service required. Single replica with single writer by design. Brief unavailability on pod rescheduling is acceptable for a non-production platform. |
| DNS / TLS | Morsel API + Let's Encrypt; Cloud DNS or Cloudflare | Fully automated; zero operator involvement in cert renewal or DNS record management. Cloudflare supported for organisations already using it as their primary DNS provider. |
| Container registry | Single private Artifact Registry repository; push isolation enforced by Morsel API | Simpler IAM than per-repo repositories. Repos never write to the canonical registry directly. Morsel API is the sole writer. |
| Registry push model | Staging handshake: GitHub Actions → staging repo → Morsel copies to canonical | GitHub Actions never touches the canonical registry. Cross-repo overwrites are impossible regardless of registry ACLs. |
| Rollback | Morsel retains current + last-healthy digest per app | Minimal storage footprint. Rollback is a Morsel-internal operation requiring no registry credential by GitHub Actions. |
| GCP credentials | Workload Identity throughout; no service account key files | Nothing to rotate, nothing to leak. Zero stored secrets for platform-level access. |
| GCP isolation | Dedicated GCP project; no cross-project IAM grants | Blast radius of a full Morsel compromise is bounded to the Morsel project. Operator's wider infrastructure is unreachable. |
| Network | Private Google Access for all GCP service traffic | GCP API endpoints unreachable from internet. Only outbound leg (GitHub Actions → GCP) traverses internet, secured by OIDC. |
| Self-hosted runners | Explicitly out of scope | Operational cost of runner lifecycle management not justified for a non-production platform. |
| Hibernation idle threshold | Per-app `idle_after` field in app declaration; platform-wide default set in wizard | Per-app gives developers control over their own cold-start tradeoff. Platform default keeps the operator in control of the baseline. |
| Morsel's own secrets | GCP Secret Manager (3–4 secrets: signing key, notification config, bootstrap config, Cloudflare token if applicable) | Morsel API accesses a fixed, small set of secrets at startup via Workload Identity + Go SDK. No database credentials required — SQLite has no auth layer. |
| Token model | Short-lived access token (JWT) + long-lived refresh token | Access token verified by signature — no DB lookup per request. Role encoded in token; changes take effect within one TTL. Refresh token rotated on every use. |
| Access token TTL | 15 minutes (operator configurable) | Short enough that role changes propagate quickly. Long enough to be practical without constant refresh. |
| GitHub Actions token | 10-minute access token, no refresh token | Workflow re-exchanges on every run. No stored credential needed. |
| Refresh token lifetime | 90 days | Practical for CLI use. Revocation is a single SQLite delete. |
| RBAC | Role encoded in token; two roles: operator and developer | Operator role determined at exchange time by matching Google identity against bootstrap-configured operator principal. Repo encoded from OIDC `repository` claim. No per-request directory lookup. |
| App naming | Unique within repo; unnamed app gets repo slug as name | Allows single-app repos to have a clean URL (`repo.apps.example.com`) while multi-app repos use `name.repo.apps.example.com`. |
| App declaration | `.morsel/` folder with `*.morsel.json` files | One file per app. Composable — add or remove apps by adding or removing files. Workflow discovers all files at deploy time. |
| Multi-app deploy | GitHub Actions matrix job, parallel, fail-fast disabled | Apps in a repo are independent. One failing deploy does not block others. |
| Upsert | Single `POST /api/repos/:slug/apps` for create and update | Caller always sends full desired state. Morsel determines from its own records whether this is a create or update. Consistent workflow regardless of app age. |
| Destructive persistence changes | Blocked by default; `?force=true` (operator only) to override | Prevents accidental data loss. Lint catches violations locally before CI. |
| Orphaned apps | Defined as apps whose GitHub repo has been deleted or archived. No automated detection — open problem. | Morsel holds no GitHub token and receives no webhook events. Operator performs periodic manual review via stale apps list in admin UI. |
| Platform abstraction | Single `Platform` interface with `GCPPlatform` and `LocalPlatform` implementations | All cloud SDK calls isolated in platform packages. Business logic has no cloud dependencies. Adding AWS or Azure support means implementing the interface — nothing else changes. |
| Bootstrap wizard | Platform-agnostic prompt/answer loop | Wizard presents prompts returned by `Platform.BootstrapPrompts()` and passes answers to `Platform.Bootstrap()`. Platform owns its own onboarding questions, OAuth flows, and resource planning. Wizard never branches on platform. |
| GitHub Actions workflow | Single copy-paste workflow file, triggered on push to default branch | Thin wrapper — authentication and dispatch only. `morsel app deploy` owns all deploy logic. Platform abstraction keeps workflow identical regardless of cloud platform. |
| `morsel app deploy` in CI | Detected via `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`, uses `Platform.DeployCredentials()` | Same command for local and CI. Platform handles credential and registry differences. No separate CI-specific command needed. |
| Backups | None — no automated backup or disaster recovery | Non-production platform. App owners responsible for data they cannot afford to lose. Recovery path documented for PV loss scenarios. |
| Platform upgrade strategy | Rolling — platform components upgraded one at a time, apps redeployed with new defaults | Apps keep running throughout. Hibernated apps updated in place without waking. No maintenance window required. |
| Upgrade failure handling | Skip and continue — failed apps listed in upgrade report, operator retries individually | A single app failure does not block platform upgrade. `morsel service upgrade retry` retries only failed apps. |
| Local Kubernetes | Detect existing cluster via kubeconfig; print instructions and exit if none found | Morsel does not install or manage a local Kubernetes. Complexity of cross-platform k3s management not justified for a developer tool. |
| Local mode scope | Full production replica | Hibernation, quotas, and approvals all enforced locally. Prevents surprises in CI that cannot be reproduced locally. |
| `morsel app deploy` | Local platform profiles only | Replaces GitHub Actions for local development. Not available against cloud instances — use GitHub Actions for those. |
| Blob storage API | `blob.morsel.internal` — GET, PUT, list with prefix and cursor | Apps never touch GCS directly. GCS naming complexity hidden. Quota enforced at API layer. Namespace isolation via pod identity. |
| Blob/database quotas | Separate independent limits per tier | Different cost profiles. Hitting one does not affect the other. Both individually overridable via approval workflow. |
| Database | Shared in-cluster Postgres, one database per app, PGBouncer sidecar | Developer sees fixed constants. Real per-app credentials held by PGBouncer sidecar, never visible to app. |
| Database isolation | Per-app Postgres user with GRANT scoped to own database only | App cannot access another app's database regardless of what it attempts. Kubernetes NetworkPolicy prevents pod-to-pod sidecar access. |
| Queue service | `queue.morsel.internal` backed by Postgres tables | No GCP Pub/Sub required. App creates queues at runtime — no declaration of queue names needed. Quota on total storage across all app queues. |
| Queue semantics | Queue only (no topics/fan-out) | Point-to-point delivery sufficient for non-production use cases. Simpler to implement and reason about. |
| App-to-app communication | Public HTTPS URLs only | No private inter-app channel. Private apps (`private: true`) act as VPC-internal services accessible to other Morsel apps. |
| Health checks | Standard Kubernetes liveness and readiness probes; defaults `/livez` and `/healthz` | Morsel configures probes and defers all behaviour to Kubernetes. Deploy success tied to rollout status. No custom Morsel probe logic. |
| Error responses | Structured JSON with `code`, `message`, `remedy`, `context` | Formatting is the client's responsibility. API provides stable machine-readable codes. `remedy` always present — no error without a path forward. |
| GitHub Actions error surfacing | Annotations for critical errors, step output for details | Annotations surface inline in GitHub UI. Full structured JSON in job log for debugging. `approval_required` emits warning annotation — job still succeeds. |
| Pod logs in errors | Not included | Developer fetches logs separately. Prevents accidental sensitive data leakage through deploy pipeline. |
| CronJob retries | Default 0 — fail fast | Developer opts in to retries explicitly via `retries` field. Failure surfaced immediately with exit code and stderr. |
| Worker hibernation | All queues must report `idle: true` | Morsel watches all queues; worker stays alive if any queue has external messages pending. |
| Self-consuming queue detection | Rolling window of last N messages; `idle: true` when 100% self-consumed | Prevents a worker from keeping itself alive by consuming its own messages. N is platform-configurable (default 100). Exposed as single `idle` boolean on queue. |
| Permanent resources | Per-resource `permanent` flag in app declaration, default false | Prevents accidental deletion of stateful resources on app or repo deletion. Removal requires two-step process enforced by lint. |
| Database engine | Postgres only | Single engine simplifies operations. |
| Destructive change guard | lint (local/CI) + operator-only `?force=true` | Lint catches destructive changes before they reach CI. Force flag is an operator escape hatch only — developers receive 403. |
| Sync endpoint | `POST /api/repos/:slug/sync` called once per workflow before deploys | Gives Morsel a complete view of declared apps at each git SHA. Enables deletion of removed apps without requiring explicit delete calls from the workflow. |
| morsel lint | CLI command with `--staged` and `--fix` flags | Designed as a pre-commit hook. Catches schema errors and permanent resource violations locally before CI. |
| Protected config | Subset of fields require operator approval before applying | Developers declare desired state freely; protected fields are queued for approval. App runs in best achievable state with currently approved config. |
| Approval granularity | Per resource field | Operator can approve a tier change independently of a quota increase. Changes reconcile as approved. |
| Approval expiry | Configurable, default 30 days | Stale approvals are automatically rejected and cleared. Developer resubmits if still needed. |
| Batch approvals | Single `POST /api/operator/approvals/batch` | Operator actions a set of approvals in one call. Approved changes per app applied in a single reconciliation pass. `ignore` defers without rejecting. |
| Admin UI authentication | GCP Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) | No password to manage or rotate. Operator authenticates with their existing Google account. |
| Operator principals | Google account or Google Group; either accepted | Groups suit organisations with a stable operator team; individuals suit smaller setups. IAP treats both identically. Managed via `morsel service operator` subcommands; no Morsel involvement in group membership. |

---

## 24. GitHub Actions workflow

Developers copy a single workflow file verbatim into their repository. No customisation is required beyond setting four repository-level variables once.

### Repository variables

Set these once per repository in GitHub → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Variables:

| Variable | Description | Provided by |
|---|---|---|
| `MORSEL_API_URL` | Morsel instance URL, e.g. `https://admin.apps.example.com` | Operator |
| `MORSEL_GCP_PROJECT` | GCP project ID of the Morsel instance | Operator |
| `MORSEL_WIF_PROVIDER` | Workload Identity Federation provider resource name | Operator |
| `MORSEL_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` | GCP service account email for GitHub Actions | Operator |

### Workflow file

Save as `.github/workflows/morsel-deploy.yml`:

```yaml
name: Deploy to Morsel

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  id-token: write   # required for GitHub OIDC token
  contents: read

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install morsel CLI
        run: |
          curl -L https://github.com/org/morsel/releases/latest/download/morsel-Linux-x86_64 \
            -o morsel && chmod +x morsel && sudo mv morsel /usr/local/bin/morsel

      - name: Deploy
        env:
          MORSEL_API_URL: ${{ vars.MORSEL_API_URL }}
          MORSEL_GCP_PROJECT: ${{ vars.MORSEL_GCP_PROJECT }}
          MORSEL_WIF_PROVIDER: ${{ vars.MORSEL_WIF_PROVIDER }}
          MORSEL_SERVICE_ACCOUNT: ${{ vars.MORSEL_SERVICE_ACCOUNT }}
        run: morsel app deploy
```

### What `morsel app deploy` does in CI

When `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`, the CLI detects it is running in CI and adapts:

1. Calls `Platform.DeployCredentials()` — on `GCPPlatform` this exchanges the GitHub OIDC token for a Morsel access token via WIF and obtains registry push credentials
2. Discovers all `*.morsel.json` files in `.morsel/`
3. Calls `POST /api/repos/:slug/sync` with the full app list
4. For each app in parallel:
   - Builds the container image using Docker (available on `ubuntu-latest`)
   - Pushes to the staging Artifact Registry repository
   - Calls `POST /api/repos/:slug/apps` with the image digest and Morsel token
5. Emits GitHub Actions annotations for errors and approval warnings
6. Exits non-zero on any deploy failure

### Job output

Successful deploy:
```
✓ Synced 3 apps (0 deleted)
✓ my-demo-app       deployed sha256:abc123
✓ worker            deployed sha256:def456
⚠ scheduler         tier change to 'medium' pending operator approval — running at 'small'
```

Failed deploy:
```
✓ Synced 3 apps (0 deleted)
✓ my-demo-app       deployed sha256:abc123
✗ worker            deploy failed — rollout timed out. Rolling back to sha256:prev456
✓ scheduler         deployed sha256:ghi789
```

### Dockerfile requirement

Each app must have a `Dockerfile` at the repository root, or declare a custom path in the app declaration (future field — not yet implemented). The workflow builds from the repository root context.

---

## 26. Iterative build plan

The platform is built incrementally. Each phase is independently useful and testable before the next begins.

| Phase | Scope |
|---|---|
| 1 — Foundation | `morsel service bootstrap`: GCP OAuth, preflight checks, wizard, GCP resource provisioning (VPC, GKE Autopilot, Artifact Registry, Secret Manager, IAM, WIF, IAP), GKE Persistent Volume for SQLite; platform secrets and bootstrap config written to Secret Manager |
| 1b — Platform abstraction | `Platform` interface: `BootstrapPrompts()`, `BootstrapPlan()`, `Bootstrap()`, `BlobStore`, `SecretStore`, `CredentialProvider`, `DNSProvider`, `CertProvider`; `GCPPlatform` and `LocalPlatform` implementations |
| 1c — Local mode | `LocalPlatform`: filesystem blob store, local secrets, no-op credentials, `*.morsel.localhost` DNS, self-signed certs, local registry, `morsel app deploy` CLI command |
| 2 — Morsel API: auth | Token exchange endpoints (`/api/token/github-oidc`, `/api/token/gcp-oidc`, `/api/token/refresh`), JWT signing, refresh token store in SQLite, RBAC middleware |
| 2b — Error handling | Structured error response model, error codes, rollback on deploy_failed, GitHub Actions annotation format |
| 3 — Morsel API: deploy | GitHub OIDC validation, sync endpoint, staging handshake, image copy + rollback slot management, repo auto-registration, quota enforcement, direct manifest apply via client-go, permanent resource handling, protected config approval workflow |
| 4 — Morsel API: networking | GKE Gateway API wiring, internal/external ingress, ACME certificate provisioning and renewal via Go ACME library, DNS record management via Cloud DNS and Cloudflare SDKs |
| 5 — Morsel API: persistence | GCS bucket provisioning (for blob service) |
| 6 — Morsel API: hibernation | Activity watcher goroutine, scale-to-zero via client-go, HTTP proxy for wake-on-request |
| 6b — morsel lint | CLI lint command: schema validation, permanent resource checks, --staged and --fix flags |
| 7 — Admin UI | Static React SPA deployed to GCS; app list, repo management, quota promotion, cost dashboard |
| 8 — Hardening | Audit logging, `morsel service bootstrap` upgrade behaviour, `morsel service upgrade retry`, `morsel service status`, `morsel service delete`, `morsel service operator` subcommands, disaster recovery note, operator handover docs |

Each phase will produce a working, reviewable increment. Design decisions specific to a phase will be captured as addenda to this document before that phase begins.

# Morsel — Vision

> **Status:** Draft · **Date:** May 2026

---

## What Morsel Is

Morsel is a self-hosted platform-as-a-service for hosting non-production applications — demos, experiments, internal tools, and integration test environments — in a dedicated GCP project. It gives developers a Heroku-style experience: push code, get a running app with a URL. It gives operators a low-maintenance system they can run part-time without cloud expertise.

The core promise is that a developer should be able to go from zero to a deployed, HTTPS-accessible application without knowing anything about Kubernetes, GCP, DNS, or certificates. The operator should be able to keep the platform running with a few hours of attention per month, without ever touching kubectl or the GCP console.

---

## Goals

- Let developers deploy containerised apps with nothing more than a git push
- Support HTTP servers, background workers, and scheduled jobs
- Provide managed persistence: blob storage, databases, and queues
- Enforce cost caps automatically via quota limits — no manual intervention for routine use
- Detect and hibernate idle apps; wake them transparently on next request
- Manage DNS and HTTPS automatically under an operator-controlled domain
- Keep apps unreachable from the public internet when required
- Allow ownership transfer of apps between repos without downtime
- Require part-time attention from a single, rotating operator

---

## Non-Goals

- **Production workloads** — Morsel has no SLA. Apps that receive real user traffic or hold data that cannot be lost belong elsewhere.
- **Multi-region or high-availability deployments** — a single GKE cluster in a single region is the target deployment model.
- **Workloads requiring GPUs or specialised hardware** — standard GKE node pools only.
- **Replacing an internal developer portal** — Morsel does not integrate with Backstage, service catalogues, or incident management tools.
- **General-purpose CI/CD** — Morsel is a deployment target, not a build system.
- **Data backup or disaster recovery** — app owners are responsible for data they cannot afford to lose. This is stated explicitly so it is never forgotten.

---

## Personas

### Developer / app owner

A member of the GitHub organisation. Deploys and operates apps on behalf of their team. No cloud or Kubernetes knowledge required or expected. Their entire interface is a git repository and `*.morsel.json` configuration files.

Developers care about: fast deploys, predictable URLs, working persistence, and clear error messages when something goes wrong.

### Operator

Manages the running platform on a part-time basis. The role may rotate. The operator has no expectation of Kubernetes or GCP knowledge. Their entire workflow is two tools: the `morsel` CLI (for installation, upgrades, and access management) and the admin UI (for day-to-day management). Routine tasks should take minutes.

The operator's task surface is deliberately narrow:
- Run `morsel service bootstrap` to install or upgrade the platform
- Review new repos that have auto-registered
- Promote repos to higher quota tiers on request
- Transfer app ownership in unusual circumstances
- Periodically review and clean up apps from deleted or archived repos
- Glance at cost and health dashboards
- Act on alerts (failed deploys, expiring certs)

### Designer / implementer

Builds and evolves the platform itself. Comfortable with Kubernetes internals and GCP. Interacts with the full stack. This role is not the operator — complexity is acceptable here because it is absorbed once during construction and rarely during maintenance.

---

## Design Principles

These principles explain the compromises made throughout the design. When a later decision seems odd in isolation, it is usually in service of one of these.

### Low, controllable dollar cost

The platform must cost little to run even when underutilised. Hibernation (scale-to-zero for idle apps) is central to this. Quota tiers bound per-repo spend. The cost dashboard gives the operator visibility without requiring them to read GCP billing directly. Every design choice that increases cost requires a proportionate justification.

### Low operator overhead

The operator role must be viable part-time, by someone without cloud expertise, and must survive rotation. This rules out: ad-hoc kubectl commands, GCP console operations, manual cert renewals, manual DNS changes, and per-app configuration managed outside the platform. If a routine operation requires the operator to consult documentation, it is a platform failure.

### Safe to run adjacent to enterprise

Morsel runs in a dedicated GCP project with no cross-project IAM grants, no GitHub credentials, and no ability to enumerate the GitHub organisation. A fully compromised Morsel cannot be used as a stepping stone into the operator's wider infrastructure. This boundary is non-negotiable — any proposed change that would expand the blast radius requires explicit designer sign-off.

### Self-service with opinionated defaults

Developers should be unblocked without operator involvement for routine operations. The first deploy from a new repo succeeds automatically. Resources have safe defaults. The operator is in the critical path only for quota increases and protected config changes. This means the defaults must be genuinely good — not minimal stubs that force every developer to ask for an upgrade.

### Few knobs

Configuration surface for developers is intentionally small. `morsel.json` has a short field list. Fields that control resource sizes go through the approval workflow. Fields that do not matter for most apps are omitted. When a reasonable default exists, it is used without exposing a knob. Developers who want more control ask the operator, not the config file.

### End-to-end solutions, not primitives

Morsel provides complete managed solutions: a working database connection with no credentials to manage, blob storage with no SDK to configure, a queue with fixed semantics. The design explicitly rejects exposing raw GCP primitives (GCS buckets, Pub/Sub topics, Cloud SQL instances) to app developers. Managed access via fixed internal hostnames with zero configuration is the goal.

### Flexibility with hosting

The `Platform` interface isolates all cloud-specific concerns. Business logic never imports a cloud SDK. `GCPPlatform` is the production implementation; `LocalPlatform` runs a full replica on a developer's machine with no cloud account required. The design anticipates future `AWSPlatform` and `AzurePlatform` implementations as a well-scoped addition, not a redesign.

---

## Security Model

These constraints are non-negotiable. They exist to ensure Morsel cannot be used as a liability for the operator's wider organisation.

**GitHub calls Morsel, not the other way around.** GitHub Actions calls the Morsel API and presents a short-lived OIDC token as proof of identity. Morsel never holds a GitHub credential of any kind.

**GCP project isolation.** Morsel runs in a dedicated GCP project. All Morsel resources live in this project and nowhere else. Morsel's GCP service accounts are granted no roles outside this project. No service account key files are created — all GCP authentication uses Workload Identity.

**Blast radius if Morsel is compromised.** An attacker who fully compromises Morsel can deploy or delete apps on the platform, exhaust quota, and access data in platform-managed persistence. They cannot enumerate the GitHub organisation, read source code, impersonate users outside the platform, or touch any GCP project other than the dedicated Morsel project. This blast radius must be preserved.

**No long-lived credentials anywhere.** No GitHub PAT, no service account keys, no stored cloud credentials. Every authentication relationship in the system uses short-lived tokens, Workload Identity, or ambient GKE identity.

---

## Key Compromises

These are the explicit tradeoffs made in service of the principles above. They are recorded here so they do not have to be re-litigated every time a component is designed.

| Compromise | Rationale |
|---|---|
| No SLA, no HA, single-region | Non-production workloads do not justify the cost and operational complexity of multi-region HA |
| No backup or disaster recovery | App owners must own their data. Building a recovery system creates a false sense of safety for production workloads that should not be on Morsel |
| No self-hosted GitHub Actions runners | Eliminates the internet leg of the GH Actions → GCP connection but introduces persistent VMs requiring patching and lifecycle management. Not justified for a non-production platform |
| Advisory database storage limits | Per-database enforcement at the Postgres level is not possible on a shared instance. Limits are tracked and enforced by Morsel at tier-change time, not at every write |
| Queue semantics only (no topics/fan-out) | Point-to-point delivery is sufficient for non-production use cases and dramatically simpler to implement and reason about |
| Orphaned app detection is manual | Morsel holds no GitHub token and receives no webhook events, so it cannot detect repo deletion automatically. Operator performs periodic manual review |
| SQLite for platform state | Morsel's own data is light. No managed database service required. Brief unavailability on pod rescheduling is acceptable for a non-production platform |
| No pod logs in error responses | Prevents accidental sensitive data leakage through the deploy pipeline. Developers fetch logs separately |

# Morsel — Architecture

> **Status:** Draft · **Date:** May 2026

---

## Overview

Morsel is built on GKE running in a dedicated non-production GCP project. All Kubernetes and GCP complexity is fully hidden from operators and developers — only the designer interacts with it directly.

The platform has four logical layers:

| Layer | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Developer experience** | `git push` triggers a deploy workflow; `morsel.json` files declare what to deploy |
| **Control plane** | The Morsel API applies manifests, manages lifecycle, enforces quotas, issues tokens, and coordinates all platform operations |
| **Runtime** | GKE runs one Kubernetes namespace per app; workloads are Deployments, CronJobs, and sidecars |
| **Platform** | Cloud-specific implementations of storage, secrets, DNS, TLS, and identity — abstracted behind the `Platform` interface |

---

## System Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ GitHub                                                              │
│                                                                     │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐              │
│  │ Developer Repo                                   │              │
│  │  .morsel/app.morsel.json                         │              │
│  │  Dockerfile                                      │              │
│  │  .github/workflows/morsel-deploy.yml             │              │
│  └──────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘              │
│                     │ git push → GitHub Actions                     │
│                     │                                               │
│  ┌──────────────────▼───────────────────────────────┐              │
│  │ morsel app deploy (in CI)                        │              │
│  │  1. Exchange OIDC token → Morsel token           │              │
│  │  2. Build container image                        │              │
│  │  3. Push to staging Artifact Registry            │              │
│  │  4. POST /api/repos/:slug/apps                   │              │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘              │
└──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────┘
                           │ HTTPS (outbound from GitHub-hosted runner)
                           ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ GCP Project: morsel-prod                                            │
│                                                                     │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │ GKE Autopilot Cluster                                       │   │
│  │                                                             │   │
│  │  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │   │
│  │  │ morsel namespace                                    │   │   │
│  │  │                                                     │   │   │
│  │  │  Morsel API ──── SQLite PV                          │   │   │
│  │  │  Blob Service ── SQLite PV (quota tracking)         │   │   │
│  │  │  Queue Service ─ Postgres (tables per queue)        │   │   │
│  │  │  Hibernation watcher (goroutine in Morsel API)      │   │   │
│  │  │  Wake-on-request HTTP proxy                         │   │   │
│  │  │  Admin UI (static bundle served from GCS)           │   │   │
│  │  │  Shared Postgres instance                           │   │   │
│  │  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │   │
│  │                                                             │   │
│  │  ┌────────────────────┐  ┌────────────────────┐            │   │
│  │  │ app namespace:     │  │ app namespace:     │  ...       │   │
│  │  │ org-my-repo        │  │ org-other-repo     │            │   │
│  │  │                    │  │                    │            │   │
│  │  │  Deployment/       │  │  Deployment/       │            │   │
│  │  │  CronJob/Worker    │  │  CronJob/Worker    │            │   │
│  │  │  PGBouncer sidecar │  │  PGBouncer sidecar │            │   │
│  │  │  ResourceQuota     │  │  ResourceQuota     │            │   │
│  │  │  LimitRange        │  │  LimitRange        │            │   │
│  │  │  NetworkPolicy     │  │  NetworkPolicy     │            │   │
│  │  └────────────────────┘  └────────────────────┘            │   │
│  │                                                             │   │
│  │  GKE Gateway API ── Internal / External Load Balancer       │   │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                     │
│  ┌──────────────────┐  ┌───────────────────┐  ┌────────────────┐  │
│  │ Artifact Registry│  │  GCS Bucket       │  │ Secret Manager │  │
│  │  staging/        │  │  blob storage     │  │  signing key   │  │
│  │  canonical/      │  │  admin UI bundle  │  │  bootstrap cfg │  │
│  └──────────────────┘  └───────────────────┘  └────────────────┘  │
│                                                                     │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐                      │
│  │ Cloud DNS / Cloudflare                   │                      │
│  │  *.apps.example.com → Load Balancer      │                      │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────┘                      │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Operator machine:
  morsel service bootstrap  ──→  GCP OAuth → provision GKE + infra
  morsel service status     ──→  GET /api/operator/status
  Browser ──→ admin.apps.example.com (IAP-protected admin UI)
```

---

## Components

### Morsel API

The control plane. A Go HTTP service running in the `morsel` namespace. All platform operations flow through it.

Responsibilities:
- OIDC token validation and Morsel token issuance
- App and repo lifecycle (create, update, delete, sync)
- Image staging handshake and registry copy
- Kubernetes manifest apply via `client-go`
- Quota enforcement and approval workflow
- Hibernation watcher and HTTP proxy for wake-on-request
- Certificate provisioning and renewal via ACME/Let's Encrypt
- DNS record management via Cloud DNS or Cloudflare
- Platform state persistence in SQLite on a GKE PersistentVolume

See [components/morsel-api.md](components/morsel-api.md).

### Bootstrap CLI (`morsel`)

A static Go binary. The operator's sole interface for installing, configuring, and upgrading the platform. No Terraform, kubectl, or gcloud required.

Responsibilities:
- GCP OAuth authentication
- Preflight checks
- Wizard-driven configuration collection
- GCP resource provisioning (GKE, Artifact Registry, Secret Manager, IAM, WIF, IAP)
- Platform upgrades (rolling)
- Operator access management
- `morsel lint` for developer `morsel.json` validation
- `morsel app deploy` for local and CI deploys

See [components/bootstrap-cli.md](components/bootstrap-cli.md).

### Blob Service (`blob.morsel.internal`)

A lightweight HTTP object storage service running in the `morsel` namespace. Apps access it via a fixed internal hostname with no SDK or credentials.

See [components/blob-service.md](components/blob-service.md).

### Queue Service (`queue.morsel.internal`)

A lightweight HTTP queue service backed by Postgres tables. Apps create queues at runtime and enqueue/dequeue via a fixed internal hostname.

See [components/queue-service.md](components/queue-service.md).

### Database Service (`database.morsel.internal`)

A shared in-cluster Postgres instance with a PGBouncer sidecar per app. Apps connect using fixed constants — no credentials visible to the developer.

See [components/database-service.md](components/database-service.md).

### Admin UI

A static React SPA served from GCS and protected by GCP Identity-Aware Proxy. The operator's web interface for day-to-day platform management.

See [components/admin-ui.md](components/admin-ui.md).

---

## Platform Abstraction

All infrastructure concerns are accessed through the `Platform` interface. Business logic never imports a cloud SDK directly. Platform-specific implementations live in isolated packages and are injected at startup.

| Implementation | Use |
|---|---|
| `GCPPlatform` | Production — GCS, Secret Manager, Workload Identity, Cloud DNS / Cloudflare, ACME/Let's Encrypt |
| `LocalPlatform` | Local development — filesystem blobs, local JSON secrets, `*.morsel.localhost`, self-signed certs |
| `AWSPlatform` | Future |
| `AzurePlatform` | Future |

See [platform/interface.md](platform/interface.md), [platform/gcp.md](platform/gcp.md), [platform/local.md](platform/local.md).

---

## Data Flows

### Deploy flow

```
Developer pushes to main branch
  → GitHub Actions triggers
  → morsel app deploy (CI mode)
      → Platform.DeployCredentials()
          → Exchange GitHub OIDC token for Morsel token via WIF
          → Obtain Artifact Registry push credentials
      → POST /api/repos/:slug/sync   (declare full app list)
      → For each app (parallel):
          → docker build
          → docker push → staging Artifact Registry
          → POST /api/repos/:slug/apps  (image digest + Morsel token)
              → Morsel API validates token
              → Morsel API copies image: staging → canonical registry
              → Morsel API deletes staging image
              → Morsel API applies Kubernetes manifest via client-go
              → Morsel API watches rollout → success or rollback
```

### Hibernation flow

```
Morsel API watcher goroutine
  → Tracks last HTTP activity per HTTP app
  → Polls queue depth for worker apps
  → On idle threshold exceeded:
      → Scale deployment to 0 via client-go
      → Activate wake-on-request proxy for HTTP apps
      → Suspend CronJob spec

Inbound HTTP request to hibernated app
  → GKE Gateway routes to wake-on-request proxy
  → Proxy holds request
  → Proxy scales deployment to 1 via Morsel API
  → Proxy waits for pod ready
  → Proxy forwards held request to pod
  → Subsequent requests route directly (proxy steps aside)
```

### Operator bootstrap flow

```
Operator runs: morsel service bootstrap
  → Phase 1: GCP OAuth browser flow → access token (memory only)
  → Phase 2: Preflight checks (billing, APIs, quota, IAM, DNS)
  → Phase 3: Wizard (first run only) → collect config → write to Secret Manager
  → Phase 4: Provision in dependency order:
      GCS state bucket → VPC → GKE cluster → Artifact Registry
